questions.explain: Functional narcissists are self-absorbed too, but a coherent self they can love keeps them from falling deep into themselves.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Greene says functional narcissists sit below the halfway mark on the scale of self-absorption.
questions.explain: Below the halfway mark is the realm of deep narcissism; functional narcissists sit above it and, though they may dip below when depressed or challenged, they inevitably rise again.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Greene finds it ironic that narcissism has come to mean self-love, since the worst narcissists have no cohesive self to love.
questions.explain: He notes that the root of deep narcissism is precisely the lack of a cohesive self to love, which makes the usual meaning of the word ironic.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: On Greene’s scale of self-absorption, people below the halfway mark enter the realm of ____ narcissism.
questions.explain: Below the halfway mark people lack the self-esteem device, so it is very hard for them to raise themselves back up and they tend to sink deeper over time.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Order these positions on Greene’s scale of self-absorption from the bottom (most self-absorbed) to the top.
items: Deep narcissist
Functional narcissist
Healthy narcissist
Empathy, complete absorption in others
questions.explain: Deep narcissists sink below the halfway mark; functional narcissists live above it; healthy narcissists hover near the top; and empathy lies at the very top and beyond.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each position on Greene’s narcissistic spectrum to its description.
pairs: Lacks a coherent self and lives below the halfway mark
Self-absorbed but held up by a self they can love
Resilient self that hovers near the top of the scale
Realm at the top and beyond: complete absorption in others
questions.explain: The scale gauges self-absorption: deep narcissists lack the self-esteem device, functional narcissists have it, healthy narcissists have a stronger one, and empathy is the outward-facing summit.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Describe Greene’s scale of narcissism and the role of the halfway mark.
questions.a: Greene imagines narcissism as a measurable scale of self-absorption. Below the halfway mark lies deep narcissism, where people lack the self-esteem device, find it very hard to rise again and tend to sink deeper over time. Above it are functional narcissists, where most of us reside: self-absorbed but resilient, dipping below when challenged yet inevitably rising. Near the top are healthy narcissists, and beyond the top lies empathy, complete absorption in others.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put the three parts of our task as students of human nature in the order Greene gives them.
items: Fully understand the phenomenon of the deep narcissist
Be honest about our own narcissistic nature
Transform ourselves into healthy narcissists
questions.explain: Greene lists understanding deep narcissists first, honesty about our own self-absorption second, and, third and most important, the transformation into the healthy narcissist.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: What is the threefold task Greene sets for students of human nature in dealing with narcissism?
questions.a: First, we must fully understand deep narcissists so we can spot the toxic types, resist being drawn into their dramas and see through narcissistic leaders. Second, we must be honest that we are all narcissists rather than pretending to be more altruistic, since denial makes change impossible. Third and most important, we must transform ourselves into healthy narcissists who can turn their attention outward.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene give as evidence that we are all narcissists?
options: We rate other people’s qualities more generously than our own
In conversation we are champing at the bit to tell our own story
We prefer people whose values differ from ours
We like people who share our ideas because they reflect our good taste
We are all prone to flattery
questions.explain: Greene points to our eagerness to talk, our liking for people who mirror our ideas and our weakness for flattery. He says the reverse of generous rating: we prize qualities because they are ours.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene’s example of assertiveness illustrates which point about our narcissism?
options: We value a quality highly simply because we have it ourselves
Assertive people are always deeper on the spectrum than timid ones
Assertiveness is a mask that hides deep insecurity
Timid people are more empathic than assertive people
questions.explain: An assertive person sees assertiveness as positive “because it is ours”, while a timid person rates it as obnoxious and values introspection; each judges by self-love.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Greene says moralizers who denounce the narcissists of the world are often the biggest narcissists of them all.
questions.explain: He says such moralizers love the sound of their own voice as they point fingers and preach, which shows that no one stands outside the spectrum.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, why must we stop denying our self-absorbed nature?
options: Admitting it is the quickest way to win others’ sympathy
Pretending to be more altruistic makes it impossible to transform ourselves
Denial pushes us below the halfway mark into deep narcissism
Others will reject us if we hide our narcissism
questions.explain: Greene argues that moving beyond functional narcissism starts with honesty; trying to seem more altruistic than others blocks any transformation.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene insist that creating a self we can love is healthy, even though we are all narcissists?
questions.a: Without a self-esteem that comes from within, we would fall into deep narcissism, so building a lovable self should carry no stigma. We are all on the spectrum of self-absorption, and those who loudly denounce narcissists are often the worst of all. The goal is not to deny self-love but, starting from honesty about it, to move beyond functional narcissism toward healthy narcissism and empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene calls the person with a stronger, more resilient sense of self, who hovers near the top of the scale, the ____ narcissist.
questions.explain: Healthy narcissists recover quickly from insults, need less validation and can laugh at their flaws, which lets them turn their attention outward.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these traits into those Greene gives to deep narcissists and to healthy narcissists.

items.t: Recovers quickly from wounds or insults
Can laugh at their own limits and flaws
Needs relatively little validation from others
Takes almost everything personally
Sees other people as self-objects
Hard pressed to focus attention outward for long

questions.explain: Healthy narcissists embrace the full picture of themselves, so their self-love is more real and they can turn outward; deep narcissists have no inner foundation and remain prickly, controlling and self-absorbed.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these into how a narcissistic leader appears to followers and what Greene says lies beneath.

items.t: Radiant self-confidence
Saying what others do not dare to say
A vision for an innovative product
Hypersensitivity to any challenge
Inability to forge a coherent structure
A need to control everyone as self-objects

questions.explain: Followers see daring, confidence and creative vision, but Greene says we must see through the façade: underneath is hypersensitivity, chaos and a need to control everything.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: What distinguishes Greene’s healthy narcissist, and where does that person’s attention go?
questions.a: Healthy narcissists have a stronger, more resilient self: they recover quickly from wounds, need less validation, accept their limits and flaws, and can laugh at slights, so their self-love is more real and complete. From this strength they turn their attention outward, either into their work, becoming great artists, creators and inventors, or toward people by developing empathy, and sometimes both.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene say about healthy narcissists who direct their love into their work?
options: Their success gives them the attention and validation they need
They never feel doubt or insecurity
Work releases them from too much self-absorption
They change careers frequently to find fresh recognition
They tend to be successful because their outward focus is intense
questions.explain: Intense focus brings success and with it validation, and work acts as a release from self-absorption. Greene admits they still have moments of doubt, and frequent job changes mark deep narcissists.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, where do our natural empathic powers first come from?
options: Our earliest preverbal bond with our mother, extended to other caregivers
The fantasy lives we build between two and five
Lessons in good manners taught to us at school
Competition with siblings for our parents’ attention
questions.explain: Greene says that as infants we sensed our mother’s every mood in a preverbal way and, unlike other primates, extended this to other caregivers; this physical empathy persists with our closest people.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Greene reports studies showing a gradual increase in self-absorption among young people since the late 1990s, with a spike since 2010.
questions.explain: The studies Greene cites show a gradual increase since the late 1970s and a much higher spike since 2000, which he largely attributes to technology and the internet.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene blame for the rising levels of narcissism and the decline of empathy?
options: Technology and the internet
Overly strict parenting styles
A culture stressing the supreme value of individual rights
Spending more time socializing online than in person
Too many face-to-face social obligations
questions.explain: Greene attributes the rise to technology, to people replacing real social interaction with online socializing, and to a culture that encourages self-involvement by prizing individual rights.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, why does constantly checking a smartphone weaken empathy?
options: Phones expose us to too many people to understand any one of them
Online contacts flatter us so much that we stop needing people
Screens damage the mirror neurons that let us mimic others
Empathy comes through quality of attention, which constant interruption prevents
questions.explain: Like any skill, empathy depends on attention; continually interrupted attention keeps drawing us back to ourselves, so “Even in a crowd, you remain essentially alone.”

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each term from Greene’s discussion of narcissism and empathy to its meaning.
pairs: Other people treated as extensions of oneself
Parents who suffocate a child with attention
Blaming others’ mistakes on character, ours on circumstances
Mimicking the gestures and posture of someone we connect with
Brain cells that fire as if we did what we watch others do
questions.explain: These terms mark the chapter’s arc: self-objects and enmeshers explain deep narcissism, while the attribution bias, chameleon effect and mirror neurons belong to the practice of empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene say the need to develop empathy is greater than ever?
questions.a: Studies show self-absorption in young people rising since the late 1970s and spiking since 2000, much of it due to technology and the internet. People spend less time in real social interaction, and attention constantly interrupted by smartphones never gains a foothold in others’ feelings, so the social muscle atrophies. A culture that prizes individual rights adds to this self-involvement, so more people cannot imagine that others think differently.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene says that, as you turn your attention outward, empathy creates its own upward, positive ____.
questions.explain: Each side of the spectrum has its own momentum: deep narcissism drags you down, while empathy brings positive feedback, better work and the attention all humans thrive on.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Explain what Greene means when he says each side of the narcissistic spectrum has its own momentum.
questions.a: Deep narcissism tends to sink you deeper, because your connection to reality lessens and you cannot develop your work or relationships. Empathy works the opposite way: as you turn attention outward, you get constant positive feedback, people want to be around you, your work improves and you gain attention without trying. As Greene puts it, “Empathy creates its own upward, positive momentum.”

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put the four components of the empathic skill set in the order Greene presents them.
items: The empathic attitude
Visceral empathy
Analytic empathy
The empathic skill
questions.explain: Greene starts with the attitude, a state of mind, then the physical attunement of visceral empathy, then information-gathering in analytic empathy, and ends with the empathic skill developed through feedback and practice.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each component of Greene’s empathic skill set to its description.
pairs: A state of mind that starts by assuming you are ignorant of people
Emotional attunement to moods, tone and body language
Gathering information on values, background and family
Steady improvement through direct and indirect feedback
questions.explain: The four components move from mindset, to physical attunement, to knowledge about a person, to practised skill checked against feedback.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these are among the four components Greene lists in the empathic skill set?
options: The empathic attitude
Moral empathy
Strategic detachment
Visceral empathy
Analytic empathy
questions.explain: The four components are the empathic attitude, visceral empathy, analytic empathy and the empathic skill; strategic detachment and moral empathy are not among them.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each person Greene mentions in the first section of chapter 2 to the point he uses them for.
pairs: Perhaps the first recorded narcissistic leader
Re-creating slaves’ horror in a ship’s hold before writing
Getting to know better a man he did not like
The craving to be appreciated as our deepest principle
questions.explain: Absalom illustrates the narcissistic leader, Haley visceral empathy, Lincoln the challenge of analytic empathy, and James the closing epigraph on our need for appreciation.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the empathic attitude, Greene says each person you meet is like an undiscovered ____, with a very particular psychological chemistry.
questions.explain: He writes that “Each person you meet is like an undiscovered country”, to be explored with an open mind rather than judged in a snap.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene names the tendency to blame our own mistakes on circumstances but others’ mistakes on their character the ____ bias.
questions.explain: The empathic attitude works against the attribution bias by first considering the circumstances that pushed a person to act, giving them the benefit of the doubt we give ourselves.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: According to Greene, the attribution bias leads us to blame others’ mistakes on circumstances and our own on our character.
questions.explain: It is the other way round: we excuse our own mistakes by circumstances but see others’ mistakes as character flaws, and the empathic attitude reverses this.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each practice of Greene’s empathic attitude to what it is meant to achieve.
pairs: Assuming you are ignorant of people
Letting go of snap judgments and categories
Hearing the other person’s point of view
Mirroring back things said or unsaid
A tremendous seductive effect on the other
questions.explain: Each practice turns attention outward: humility replaces snap judgments, listening replaces talking, mirroring shows deep attention, and looking at circumstances gives others the indulgence we give ourselves.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Your colleague misses an important deadline and your first thought is that she is lazy. What would Greene’s empathic attitude have you do?
options: First consider what circumstances might have pushed her into the mistake
Trust your first impression, since snap judgments are usually accurate
Mirror her body language until she admits the real reason
Ask yourself which narcissistic type she belongs to
questions.explain: Seeing her lapse as a character flaw is the attribution bias; the empathic attitude gives others the same benefit of the doubt we give ourselves by considering circumstances first.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene say adopting the empathic attitude depends on the quality of your self-love?
options: Only people who love themselves deserve to be understood
Feeling superior or insecure makes your absorption in people shallow
Self-love lets you mirror others without any distance
Self-love removes all your natural biases about people
questions.explain: If you feel superior or are gripped by insecurities, your empathy stays shallow; accepting your whole character, flaws included, gives the inner strength to turn outward.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: What does Greene mean by the empathic attitude, and how can it be practised in daily conversations?
questions.a: The empathic attitude is a state of mind: instead of assuming you understand people and categorizing them quickly, you assume you are ignorant and biased and treat each person as an undiscovered country. In conversation you reverse the impulse to talk, cut off your inner monologue, give full attention and mirror back what was said or left unsaid. You give others the indulgence you give yourself, countering the attribution bias, and you work from an accepting self-love that lets slights wash over you.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene’s visceral empathy, what should you try to detect in each encounter before even paying attention to what people say?
options: The category of narcissist they most resemble
The logical consistency of their arguments
Their feeling tone, shown in voice, gestures and posture
Their family background and relationship to their parents
questions.explain: Greene says feelings and moods are easier to read than thoughts, so you attend first to the feeling tone, which registers in your own physical response.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Someone who has always ignored you suddenly shows intense interest in your life, but the attention feels unreliable. How does Greene’s visceral empathy read this?
options: They probably intend to ask something of you or use you
They have finally recognized your unique qualities
They are mirroring you to show genuine rapport
They are a healthy narcissist turning attention outward
questions.explain: Greene advises looking past interested words to the feeling tone, such as depth of listening and eye contact; if the sudden attention seems unreliable, they probably mean to manipulate you.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene says visceral empathy depends largely on ____, which fire in our brain when we watch someone do something just as if we were doing it ourselves.
questions.explain: Mirror neurons let us put ourselves in others’ shoes, which is why people high in empathy tend to be excellent mimics.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Greene reports that people who score high on tests of empathy are generally excellent mimics.
questions.explain: Such people unconsciously imitate others’ expressions, such as a smile or a wince, which gives them a feel for what others are feeling.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Before writing Roots, Alex Haley spent time working in a cotton field to re-create what slaves experienced.
questions.explain: Greene says Haley spent time in the dark interior of a ship to re-create the claustrophobic horror slaves must have felt, a visceral connection that let him write himself into their world.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene calls the tendency of people who are connecting to mimic each other’s gestures and posture the ____ effect.
questions.explain: You can induce the chameleon effect deliberately by mimicking someone, nodding and smiling, which draws out an empathic response.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these cautions does Greene give about practising visceral empathy?
options: Keep nodding, smiling and mirroring subtle and hard to detect
Absorb the other’s emotions completely to analyze them better
Maintain a degree of distance rather than become enmeshed
Mirror people as obviously as possible so they notice
Overdoing the mirroring can create a creepy effect
questions.explain: Greene warns that complete enmeshment makes analysis hard and costs control, and that obvious mirroring feels creepy, so it must be subtle.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How does Greene’s visceral empathy work, and how can you deepen it?
questions.a: Visceral empathy is emotional attunement: since moods are easier to read than thoughts, you attend to people’s feeling tone in voice, gestures and posture, notice how it registers in your own body, and read the intentions behind it. It relies on mirror neurons, so you can deepen it by mimicking expressions or recalling similar experiences, as Alex Haley did in a ship’s hold. Mirroring others subtly, through the chameleon effect, nodding and reflecting their mood, creates rapport, but you must keep some distance and avoid being obvious.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene say physical empathy must be supplemented by analytic empathy?
options: We understand people deeply only when we have information about them
Mimicking others eventually makes them distrust us
Feelings are always harder to read than thoughts
Physical empathy works only with strangers, not friends
questions.explain: We understand friends and partners well because we know their tastes, values and background, and first impressions often need adjusting once we learn more.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In analytic empathy, Greene quotes Abraham Lincoln: I don’t like that man. I must get to ____ him better.
questions.explain: Lincoln’s remark captures Greene’s advice to treat people we resist or dislike as a challenge to understand rather than as a category to judge.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene’s analytic empathy, match each piece of information to what it helps reveal.
pairs: Their early years with parents and siblings
The values they hold about strength and weakness
A rebellious or a submissive streak
A great deal about their past
questions.explain: Greene says values form mostly in the earliest years, current family ties speak volumes about the past, attitudes to authority show rebelliousness or submission, and trigger points mark sensitivity.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Your friend is repelled when a man cries in a film, while you find it touching. According to Greene’s analytic empathy, what explains the difference?
options: Your friend is a deep narcissist and you are a healthy one
Your friend is showing the attribution bias toward the actor
Values about strength and weakness formed in each person’s early years
Your friend lacks the mirror neurons that you possess
questions.explain: Greene uses this very contrast: one woman sees a crying man as sensitive, another as weak, because such values are set in the earliest years and shaped by parents.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these practices into visceral empathy and analytic empathy, as Greene describes them.

items.t: Reading the feeling tone in voice and posture
Subtly mimicking someone’s gestures
Recalling a similar experience to feel their emotion
Learning about someone’s relationship to their parents
Asking open-ended questions about their past
Understanding their culture from within their experience

questions.explain: Visceral empathy works through bodily attunement and mimicry; analytic empathy works through conversation and gathering information about values, background and culture.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what does analytic empathy involve, and with whom is it especially useful?
questions.a: Analytic empathy means gathering information, mostly through conversation, that lets you get inside another person’s spirit: their values formed in early years, their relationship to parents and siblings, their reactions to authority, their taste in partners and their trigger points. It is especially useful with people we resist or find hard to identify with, whom we would otherwise judge and categorize. The goal is to find out what makes each person unique and different from yourself.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene suggest when someone is reluctant to talk about themselves during analytic empathy?
options: Begin with a sincere admission of your own to build trust
Wait until they bring up their childhood unprompted
Press them with direct questions about their faults
Ask open-ended questions
questions.explain: Greene recommends open-ended questions or a sincere admission of your own, and adds that people generally love to talk about themselves and their past.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what are the two forms of feedback that show you are improving the empathic skill?
options: Feedback from mirror neurons, and feedback from the chameleon effect
Written feedback from friends, and spoken feedback from strangers
Direct feedback by asking, and indirect feedback by sensing greater rapport
Praise from authority figures, and criticism from rivals
questions.explain: In the direct form you discreetly ask people whether you guessed their thoughts and feelings correctly; in the indirect form you sense greater rapport and see which techniques have worked.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these into what Greene says strengthens empathy and what he says weakens it.

items.t: Interacting with many different people in the flesh
Keeping your ideas about people in flow
Watching people as they interact with others
Attention continually interrupted by a smartphone
Snap judgments that put people into categories
Socializing online instead of face to face

questions.explain: Greene says live, varied contact and judgments that never quite settle sharpen the skill, while interrupted attention, categorizing and online substitutes atrophy the social muscle.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each piece of Greene’s advice for building the empathic skill to its reason.
pairs: Interact with more people in the flesh
You simply get better at reading people
Meet a greater variety of people
Your ideas never settle into a fixed judgment
People differ depending on whom they are with
questions.explain: Greene treats empathy as a process: quantity and variety of live contact, ongoing attention and observing people in other relationships all add cues to their psychology.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How does Greene say you can develop and check your empathic skill over time?
questions.a: Greene treats empathy as a process that needs feedback, either direct, by discreetly asking people whether you read them correctly, or indirect, by sensing greater rapport. You improve by interacting with many and varied people in the flesh, keeping your ideas about them in flow rather than settled judgments, watching how they change and how they act with others, and continually mixing the visceral with the analytic. The reward is a smoother ride through life with fewer conflicts and misunderstandings.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: The chapter’s first section closes with William James: The deepest principle of Human Nature is the craving to be ____.
questions.explain: James’s line echoes the section’s starting point, that all humans have a never-ending need for attention and recognition.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: What does the chapter title Transform Self-love into Empathy signal about Greene’s view of narcissism?
options: Empathy must replace any self-image we have built
Self-love is a disorder that only deep narcissists suffer from
Self-love is not to be stamped out but redirected outward toward others
Self-love and empathy can never exist in the same person
questions.explain: Greene calls a lovable self healthy and necessary; the aim is to move from functional to healthy narcissism and turn that strength outward into empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which later chapter of the book most directly continues the theme of narcissistic leaders whose success inflates their grandiose tendencies?
options: Advance with a Sense of Purpose (The Law of Aimlessness)
Meditate on Our Common Mortality (The Law of Death Denial)
Know Your Limits (The Law of Grandiosity)
Elevate Your Perspective (The Law of Shortsightedness)
questions.explain: Greene says the narcissistic leader’s success only “inflates their grandiose tendencies”, which is the subject of the chapter on the Law of Grandiosity.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does the section The Narcissistic Spectrum end with the four components of the empathic skill set?
options: The diagnosis of narcissism is meant to lead to a practical remedy, empathy
Empathy is presented only as a defense against narcissistic leaders
Greene wants to show that empathy is a form of deep narcissism
The components summarize the four narcissistic types that follow
questions.explain: The section moves from the need for attention, through the scale of narcissism, to the most important task, transforming into a healthy narcissist and building empathy, so it closes with how to do that.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these chapters of the book in their order.
items: Master Your Emotional Self
Transform Self-love into Empathy
See Through People’s Masks
Determine the Strength of People’s Character
questions.explain: The Law of Narcissism is chapter 2, after the Law of Irrationality and before the Laws of Role-playing and Compulsive Behavior.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each idea in the first half of chapter 2 to the chapter of the book it links to.
pairs: Looking for trigger points during analytic empathy
People present a mask that we mistake for reality
Empathy lets us gently lower people’s resistance
Soften People’s Resistance by Confirming Their Self-opinion
Deep narcissists’ vicious bouts of envy
questions.explain: Greene refers back to chapter 1 for trigger points, and the chapter’s talk of masks, lowering resistance and envy is developed in the Laws of Role-playing, Defensiveness and Envy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How does the short statement of the Law of Narcissism at the chapter’s start preview the rest of the chapter?
questions.a: The statement names empathy as our great social tool, says it is blunted by self-absorption, and declares that we are all narcissists on a spectrum. It sets a twofold mission: to turn our sensitivity outward toward others and to recognize the toxic narcissists among us. The Narcissistic Spectrum section develops both, explaining deep narcissists and narcissistic leaders and then the path through healthy narcissism to empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene explain deep narcissists in detail before turning to the healthy narcissist and empathy?
questions.a: Deep narcissists make visible the self-esteem thermostat that the rest of us take for granted, so they explain how the self works. Understanding them is also the first part of our threefold task, since toxic narcissists and narcissistic leaders can do great harm. With that picture in place, Greene can ask us to admit our own narcissism and then show the upward path to healthy narcissism and empathy, which the Four Examples section goes on to illustrate.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Complete Control Narcissist example, what did Joseph Stalin encourage his lieutenants to do early in his reign, despite being older than most of them?
options: Call him by a formal title at every meeting
Report on each other's loyalty once a week
Address him with the familiar form of “you” in Russian
Submit written requests before seeing him in person
questions.explain: Early on Stalin seemed surprisingly charming and accessible, even urging his lieutenants to use the familiar form of address. The formality and distance in the other choices describe the opposite of his early manner.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene's account of Stalin, what did Sergey Kirov do in 1934 when regional leaders offered to make him premier in a coup?
options: He secretly agreed and waited for the right moment
He fled Moscow to avoid being drawn into the plot
He refused but kept the offer to himself
He revealed the plot to Stalin, who thanked him profusely
questions.explain: Kirov stayed loyal and told Stalin of the plot. Yet the disclosure revealed that Kirov was more liked than Stalin, and Stalin's manner toward him turned cold from then on.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Stalin example, why did Kirov's increasingly fulsome public praise of Stalin fail to protect him?
options: Stalin never heard the speeches in which Kirov praised him
Stalin thought the praise was too mild and grudging
Other Politburo members denounced Kirov as a flatterer
It made Stalin more suspicious, as if Kirov were trying too hard to hide the truth
questions.explain: Greene says the extra praise only made Stalin more suspicious. For a complete control narcissist, effort to soothe his insecurity can itself look like a cover-up.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene's portrait of Stalin, why did later speakers repeat a word exactly as Stalin had mispronounced it?
options: They meant to mock him quietly among themselves
Pravda printed his version as the correct form
Party rules fixed the official pronunciation of terms
Saying it correctly would make Stalin feel he was being corrected
questions.explain: One lieutenant admitted that saying the word right would have made Stalin feel corrected, which could prove suicidal. It shows how fully his sense of infallibility controlled those around him.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Stalin example, what double bind did his generals face as war with Hitler approached?
options: Speaking their minds could insult him, yet deferring to him could send him into a rage
Reporting losses angered him, yet hiding them counted as treason
Retreating angered him, yet advancing wasted the troops he valued
Asking for supplies offended him, yet going without lost battles
questions.explain: Greene says that if generals spoke their mind Stalin could be insulted, but if they deferred he would fly into a rage at their yes-saying. Nothing they did could please him.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene's account of Stalin's late-night dinners, what did Greene call “the ultimate form of control”?
options: Seating each guest according to rank
Keeping his own drinks heavily diluted
Making them watch films until dawn
Ordering his lieutenants to dance while he watched and laughed
questions.explain: Stalin made Khrushchev dance the gopak and had others slow dance together, the puppet master choreographing their every move. The diluted drinks were a tactic to watch them, not the climax Greene describes.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene's interpretation of the Complete Control Narcissist, what is the great riddle that Stalin and his type present?
options: How people so deeply narcissistic can also be so charming and gain influence through it
Why they prefer politics to business careers
How they manage to hide their troubled childhoods
Why their followers never rebel against them
questions.explain: Greene asks how such self-obsessed people can connect with and mesmerize others. His answer lies in the early part of their careers, before they turn paranoid and vicious.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what drives a complete control narcissist to listen to people with such deep attention?
options: A need to control people and discover weaknesses to play on
A wish to be liked by everyone they meet
A sincere need to connect with others
Simple curiosity about how other people live
questions.explain: Their hypersensitivity lets them mimic empathy, but from within they are impelled by the need to control and manipulate, not to connect. They probe you for weaknesses.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Greene's analysis of complete control narcissists, what pattern does he compare to the push and pull of the coquette?
options: Promises of promotion followed by sudden demotion
Long silences followed by bursts of confession
Public praise followed by private criticism
A display of attention and affection followed by an inevitable coldness
questions.explain: They pull you in with attention, then lure you deeper with coldness, so that you wonder what you did wrong and want to regain the warmth. Combined with high confidence, this can be devastatingly seductive.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How does Greene say Joseph Stalin died?
options: He died in his sleep after a long illness
He was poisoned by a member of his inner circle
After a stroke, none of his lieutenants dared to help him or call a doctor
He was shot by a lone gunman outside his office
questions.explain: Stalin died from the neglect of lieutenants who had come to fear and loathe him. Greene uses this to show that people rebel even when cowed, because free will cannot be stamped out.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, how can you see through a complete control narcissist when they first apply their charm?
options: By asking them directly about their intentions
By flattering them before they flatter you
By using visceral empathy to sense the coldness and how attention flows back to them
By challenging them openly in front of others
questions.explain: Greene says their interest is never deep or lasting and is followed by a coquettish pullback. If you stop being distracted by the charm, visceral empathy lets you sense that coldness.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what warning sign might you find in the past of a complete control narcissist?
options: A habit of openly admitting mistakes
No single deep, intimate relationship in which they exposed vulnerability
A wide circle of lifelong close friends
A long career in a single organization
questions.explain: Greene advises looking at their past for the absence of any deep relationship showing vulnerability, and for signs of a troubled childhood such as Stalin's.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Theatrical Narcissist example, why had Jeanne de Belciel made many enemies in her previous convent?
options: Through stealing from the other sisters
Through refusing to do her share of work
Through her continual sarcasm
Through spreading heretical ideas
questions.explain: Greene notes that in her previous house she had made a lot of enemies with her continual sarcasm and air of superiority, which is why her angelic behaviour at Loudun surprised the prioress.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How did Jeanne de Belciel win the favour of the prioress at Loudun?
options: By using her family's influence in the church
By reporting miracles and visions from her first week
By acting like an angel, helping with daily tasks, and becoming the house expert on mystical theology
By exposing the misconduct of the other sisters
questions.explain: Given books on Saint Teresa and mysticism, Jeanne made a complete show of knowledge and piety. The miracles came only later, after she had become prioress.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Loudun affair described by Greene, what happened to the priest Urbain Grandier?
options: He confessed and retired to a monastery
He was condemned for sorcery and burned at the stake
He was acquitted and became director of the house
He was exiled from France
questions.explain: Although he had never set foot in the house or met Jeanne, Grandier was charged with sorcery, tortured, and burned at the stake in 1634.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene's interpretation, why did Jeanne alone keep her demons after Grandier's execution?
options: Her possession was genuine and harder to cure
The other nuns blamed her and isolated her
The Jesuits ordered her to stay possessed
She found the sudden lack of attention unbearable and upped the ante
questions.explain: While the other nuns felt guilt over an innocent man's death, Jeanne felt only the loss of attention. Refusing to let go of the demons kept her at the center of the spectacle.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, how did Jeanne de Belciel learn to display such convincing signs of possession?
options: She devoured a book on demonology and gave herself its most dramatic traits
She copied the behaviour of another possessed nun
She drew on her earlier reading about Saint Teresa
Canon Mignon coached her before each exorcism
questions.explain: Soon after the exorcists arrived she was given a book on demonology, and knowing its details she displayed the traits the exorcists would read as sure signs of possession.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Drawing on the Theatrical Narcissist example, why does Greene say deep narcissism often goes unnoticed until it becomes extreme?
options: Deep narcissists are masters of disguise who use their lack of a coherent self to play many parts
Other people are too busy to observe anyone closely
Deep narcissists are too rare to be recognized
Deep narcissists avoid company and stay hidden
questions.explain: They sense early that revealing their need for attention would repel people, so they disguise it through dramatic devices. Their lack of a coherent self becomes an advantage.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Narcissistic Couple example, why did Leo Tolstoy give Sonya his diaries before their wedding?
options: So she could start copying his writing for publication
So she would understand he was happily forsaking his old ways for a new life with her
To find a reason to call off the marriage
To test whether she would stay loyal to him
questions.explain: Tolstoy wanted no secrets between them and meant the diaries as honesty. Sonya, from a conventional household, read them instead as a sign he regretted his proposal.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene's interpretation of the Tolstoys, what generally makes a relationship narcissistic?
options: A large difference in wealth or status
A large difference in the partners' ages
A lack of empathy that makes both partners retreat deeper into defensive positions
One partner being a deep narcissist
questions.explain: Greene stresses that a relationship has a life of its own, and it is the dynamic of missing empathy, not just one person's traits, that makes it narcissistic.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what is the key to employing empathy within a relationship such as the Tolstoys' marriage?
options: Understanding the other person's value system, which inevitably differs from yours
Keeping a careful record of each other's faults
Avoiding any discussion of deeply held beliefs
Giving in to the other person on every disputed issue
questions.explain: What a partner reads as love or generosity diverges from your own way of thinking, and these values form in early childhood. Keeping them in mind lets you enter their perspective just when you would turn defensive.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Healthy Narcissist example, what did Shackleton see as the greatest danger after abandoning the Endurance?
options: The harsh winter weather
The drifting currents under the ice floe
The morale of the men
The dwindling food supplies
questions.explain: Of all the obstacles, the one that filled him with the most dread was morale: a few malcontents could spread negativity until it became every man for himself.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Shackleton example, how did Shackleton handle Harry McNeish when he suddenly stopped rowing on the voyage?
options: He stopped the boat and had hot milk boiled for everyone, saying they were all tired
He ordered him sharply to keep rowing
He took McNeish's place at the oar himself
He made a joke at McNeish's expense to shame him
questions.explain: Shackleton sensed that yelling would make McNeish more rebellious. Treating everyone spared McNeish the embarrassment of being singled out.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Drawing on Shackleton's story, what does Greene say is what makes us develop our empathic powers?
options: Growing older
Natural talent
Necessity
Formal education
questions.explain: Greene writes that if we feel our survival depends on gauging the moods and minds of others, we find the focus to tap into these powers, as Shackleton did on the ice.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In Chapter 2, why does Greene place Shackleton, the healthy narcissist, last among the four examples?
options: He models the outward-turned empathy the chapter urges, after three types that show where narcissism goes wrong
He illustrates the narcissistic couple in a working relationship
He is the most dangerous type, so he forms the climax of the warnings
His story is the oldest, so the examples run in time order
questions.explain: The first three examples are cautionary (control, theatre, a narcissistic relationship); Shackleton shows the healthy narcissist and ends with how we should develop the same skills. The examples are not in date order, since Jeanne's story is the oldest.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: In Greene's account, Stalin's own drinks were heavily diluted during the all-night drinking bouts at which he watched his lieutenants.
questions.explain: Stalin forced his lieutenants to drink more so they would lose self-control, while his own drinks were watered down so he could watch them.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: In Greene's account, Sergey Kirov was executed after a public show trial in December 1934.
questions.explain: Kirov was assassinated by a lone gunman outside his office. No one could directly implicate Stalin, though the killing almost certainly had his tacit approval.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: According to Greene, Vladimir Lenin tried on his deathbed to warn others about Stalin's lethal nature, but his warnings went unheeded.
questions.explain: Greene uses Lenin as an example of listening to people who have seen a complete control narcissist's true nature and tried to warn others.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: In the Theatrical Narcissist example, the names that appeared as Jeanne's stigmata were on the palm of her right hand.
questions.explain: They appeared on her left hand, which Greene finds suspicious because it was where she could most easily write them herself.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: According to Greene, Jeanne de Belciel later wrote an autobiography admitting a theatrical side to her personality while maintaining that the final miracle was real.
questions.explain: She admitted to continually playing a part but insisted the last miracle was sincere. Many sisters who saw her daily called her a consummate actress.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: According to Greene, Leo Tolstoy's mother died when he was ten, leaving a hole he tried to fill with affairs.
questions.explain: Greene says his mother died when he was two, leaving a giant hole he could never fill, one of the signs of his deep narcissism.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: In Chapter 2, the four examples move from types to beware of toward a healthy narcissist offered as a model to follow.
questions.explain: Stalin, Jeanne de Belciel and the Tolstoys show deep narcissism in a leader, a performer and a relationship; Shackleton shows the healthy narcissist whose empathy the reader should copy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: Near South Georgia Island, Shackleton lost his composure and swung wildly at a crew member who had stopped rowing.
questions.explain: His single outburst was aimed at a small bird hovering over the boat. He felt embarrassed at once and soon made a joke at his own expense.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: In the Shackleton example, Shackleton spread Frank Hurley and Huberht Hudson among different tents to dilute their influence.
questions.explain: He brought both Hurley and Hudson into his own tent so he could attend to them and keep an eye on them. It was other suspected malcontents he spread among different tents.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: True or false: According to Greene, the pattern of mutual misunderstanding set by Tolstoy's diaries lasted for forty-eight years of marriage.
questions.explain: Greene says the couple fell into hardened positions after the diary episode that lasted for forty-eight years.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these did Stalin do early in his reign that made people feel part of his inner circle?
options: Put his arm around you as he walked you out of his office
Insisted on being addressed by a formal title
Listened with intense interest, his eyes boring into you
Handed out medals at the end of each meeting
Sang and told earthy jokes
questions.explain: Greene describes Stalin's intense listening, his intimate farewells and his entertaining songs and jokes. Far from insisting on formality, he urged even younger men to use the familiar form of address.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these were ways Stalin's lieutenants tried to avoid making him anxious?
options: Looking him in the eye, but not for too long
Mixing in a touch of bluntness while largely deferring
Politely declining his dinner invitations
Taking notes when he talked, but not writing down everything
Agreeing with every opinion he expressed
questions.explain: Reading Stalin became an arcane science of balance. Constant agreement enraged him, and his dinner invitations were impossible to refuse.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene advise for recognizing a complete control narcissist?
options: Listen to people who have seen their true nature and tried to warn others
Judge them by their public displays of modesty
Trust the warmth they show you at first meeting
Look for the absence of any deep, intimate relationship in their past
Notice the terrified expressions of those who serve them daily
questions.explain: Greene points to their past, the fear of those around them, and the warnings of people like Lenin. Their early warmth and outward modesty are exactly what mislead people.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these did Jeanne de Belciel do while Father Surin was exorcising her?
options: Refused to speak with Surin
Slept on the hard floor
Had potions of wormwood poured over her food
Asked to be transferred to another convent
questions.explain: She took an unusual liking to Surin, kept him for hours of spiritual talk, and gave up all luxuries. Avoiding him is the opposite of what she did.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these disguises does Greene say theatrical narcissists use to hide their need for attention?
options: Refusing any public notice or praise
Reveling in their status as a victim
Making a show of supporting the right cause
Avoiding all drama so as to blend in
questions.explain: They go further than anyone in seeming moral, or in the opposite direction pose as victims. Either way the focus stays on them; blending in would defeat their purpose.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these did Sonya see as Tolstoy's hypocrisy after his spiritual crisis?
options: He gave up writing diaries so she could not read them
He gave up his property rights but kept living like a lord and asking her for money
He vowed celibacy yet kept making her pregnant
He dressed like a peasant but travelled in a luxury private railway coach when ill
questions.explain: Greene lists these three contradictions. Tolstoy kept writing diaries, which Sonya insisted on reading, even on the sly.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene give as signs that Leo Tolstoy was a deep narcissist?
options: His mother died when he was two, leaving a hole he could never fill
He felt continually disgusted with himself and unsure who he was
He behaved recklessly in his youth, as if this could make him feel whole
He was raised by an enmeshing father who never left his side
questions.explain: Greene cites the early loss of his mother, his reckless youth and his fragmented sense of self. No enmeshing father appears in the account.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these did Shackleton do to keep up morale while the crew camped on the ice floe?
options: Drew up a varied daily duty roster with simple goals
Served hot tea the first morning and kept the mood light
Explained his detailed escape plans on the first morning
Organized sporting events and night-time entertainments
questions.explain: Shackleton thought discussing escape ideas at the start would make the men too anxious, so he let them feel his optimism through his manner instead.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these individual signals did Shackleton read to judge each man's emotional state?
options: What they wrote in letters home
Their tone of voice
How many hours they slept
How quickly they ate their food
How slowly they rose out of bed
questions.explain: Greene lists tone of voice, eating speed and slowness in rising. Letters and hours of sleep are not mentioned.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Which of these does Greene present as parts of Shackleton's model for reading people?
options: Scolding malcontents so others would not copy them
Dividing his attention almost equally between individuals and the group
Leaving morale to his officers so he could plan the escape
Understanding the primary role his own attitude played in the group's mood
Being gentle when he detected dips in spirit or negativity
questions.explain: Greene lays out these three steps. Scolding would make people feel ashamed and singled out, with contagious effects down the road.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene's first narcissistic type, illustrated by Joseph Stalin, is the Complete ____ Narcissist.
questions.explain: The type is defined by control: of their own emotions, of your reactions, and finally of who is in, who is out, who lives and who dies.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Stalin example, Sergey Kirov was a powerful member of the ____ and Stalin's closest friend after his wife's suicide.
questions.explain: Kirov was a powerful Politburo member and Stalin's confidant, which made his growing popularity so dangerous.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: At his late-night dinners Stalin made Nikita Khrushchev dance the ____, a strenuous dance with much squatting and kicking.
questions.explain: Making Khrushchev dance the gopak, which often left him sick, was part of what Greene calls the puppet master choreographing every move.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Because they are so sensitive to slights, complete control narcissists can listen deeply and ____ empathy, though they are driven by control.
questions.explain: Greene says they can mimic empathy; the difference is that inside they are impelled by the need to control rather than connect.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene warns that complete control narcissists are like ____: once you are too close, you cannot get away and they will devour you.
questions.explain: His advice, if you suspect this type, is to keep your distance before you are drawn in.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Theatrical Narcissist example, Jeanne de Belciel claimed in her dreams to be visited and assaulted by the parish priest Urbain ____.
questions.explain: Grandier had politely declined Jeanne's invitation to direct the house, and he was later burned at the stake as a sorcerer.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: The Jesuits sent Father Jean-Joseph ____ to exorcise Jeanne de Belciel once and for all.
questions.explain: Surin wanted badly to be the one to redeem her, which Greene says made him fall for the simplest of miracles.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: After her miracles and tour of Europe, Jeanne de Belciel became known as Jeanne des ____.
questions.explain: As Jeanne des Anges her head was mummified after death and displayed at Loudun next to the anointed chemise.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene warns that theatrical narcissists play on your ____, drawing you into their drama.
questions.explain: By posing as moral heroes or victims they exploit your empathy, then consume you with their needs.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Out of bitterness at Sonya's materialistic ways, Tolstoy wrote the novella The ____ Sonata, based on their marriage.
questions.explain: The Kreutzer Sonata painted Sonya in the worst light, part of the escalating cycle between them.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In interpreting the Tolstoys, Greene says a relationship has a life and ____ all its own.
questions.explain: This is why he looks at how each side shapes the other rather than only at individual traits.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Shackleton ordered the abandonment of the ship ____ after it had been trapped in Antarctic ice for over eight months.
questions.explain: Losing the Endurance ended his dream of the first land crossing of Antarctica and made the men's survival his only goal.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: From Elephant Island, Shackleton and five men sailed a small boat about eight hundred miles to South ____ Island.
questions.explain: South Georgia was the most accessible inhabited land, and the whalers there helped rescue the men left on Elephant Island.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Greene's fourth example is titled The Healthy Narcissist—the ____ Reader.
questions.explain: Shackleton is the healthy narcissist because his skill lay in reading the shifting moods of individuals and the group.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Chapter 2 of The Laws of Human Nature is subtitled The Law of ____.
questions.explain: The four examples illustrate the Law of Narcissism, showing deep narcissists to beware of and the healthy narcissist to become.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these events in the Kirov story in the order Greene tells them.
items: Regional leaders offer Kirov the premiership
Kirov reveals the plot to Stalin
Stalin turns cold toward Kirov
Kirov praises Stalin more fulsomely in public
A lone gunman kills Kirov
questions.explain: Kirov's loyalty exposed his popularity, Stalin cooled, Kirov's efforts to soothe him only raised suspicion, and in December 1934 he was assassinated.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these stages of Stalin's rule in the order Greene describes them.
items: Kirov is assassinated
The great purge of the late 1930s
Stalin oversees every war detail and fires his best generals
Post-war dinners with forced drinking and dancing
A stroke, and death from his lieutenants' neglect
questions.explain: Greene traces a growing need for control from Kirov's death through the purge and the war to the dinners, ending with lieutenants too afraid to help him.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these stages in the career of a complete control narcissist in the order Greene describes.
items: Charm through deep attention
A coquettish coldness that pulls you in deeper
Resentment at having to play the charm game
Turning against former friends
Micromanaging everything, trusting no one
questions.explain: Greene says their danger lies at the start, when they charm; as they grow secure in power they resent courting others, turn on friends and end as micromanagers.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these stages in Jeanne de Belciel's story in order.
items: Arrives at Loudun as a new sister
Becomes prioress at twenty-five
Reports dreams of Grandier
Stars in the public exorcisms
Shows stigmata under Surin's care
Tours Europe displaying her miracles
questions.explain: Each stage raised the level of attention Jeanne received, from the prioress's favour to crowds of thousands.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put the names that appeared on Jeanne de Belciel's left hand in the order they appeared.
items: Joseph
Jesus
Mary
questions.explain: Joseph appeared first and faded after several days, replaced by Jesus, then Mary, then other names.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these events in the Tolstoys' marriage in order.
items: Tolstoy shows Sonya his diaries
Tolstoy's spiritual crisis at fifty
Tolstoy writes The Kreutzer Sonata
Sonya walks out into the snow to die
Tolstoy steals away from home at night
Tolstoy dies in a stationmaster's cottage
questions.explain: The diary episode before the wedding set the pattern; the crisis, novella and suicide attempts sharpened it until Tolstoy fled in 1910 and died soon after.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put these stages of the Endurance survival story in order.
items: Shackleton orders the ship abandoned
The crew camps on the drifting ice floe
The lifeboats reach Elephant Island
Six men sail to South Georgia Island
The men on Elephant Island are rescued
questions.explain: The ice floe grew dangerously small, forcing the move to Elephant Island; the small-boat voyage then brought help from the whalers on South Georgia.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Put Chapter 2's four examples of narcissistic types in the order Greene presents them.
items: The Complete Control Narcissist
The Theatrical Narcissist
The Narcissistic Couple
The Healthy Narcissist—the Mood Reader
questions.explain: Greene moves from the most dangerous leader type, through the performer and the narcissistic relationship, to the healthy narcissist as the model.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each narcissistic type in Chapter 2 to the figure Greene uses to illustrate it.
questions.explain: Each historical figure illustrates one point on the narcissistic spectrum, from toxic control to healthy empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each name in Greene's Stalin story to its role.
pairs: Tried on his deathbed to warn about Stalin
questions.explain: These figures show Stalin's envy, his humiliation of lieutenants, the unheeded warning, and the cult he claimed not to want.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each person in the Loudun story to their part in it.
pairs: Confessor who hated Grandier and called in exorcists
Priest burned at the stake for sorcery
Jesuit who longed to be the one to redeem her
Kissed the fragrant chemise in Paris
questions.explain: Jeanne sensed the hidden desires of each person around her and played on them to win attention.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each member of Shackleton's crew to how Shackleton handled him.
pairs: Asked for his opinion and put in Shackleton's tent
Talked with more than anyone else
Put in charge of fitting out the boat
Given lighter but equally important tasks
Spared from killing his own pet cat
questions.explain: Shackleton treated each man according to his particular psychology, from Hurley's need to feel important to the physicist's flagging spirit.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each explorer to the strength Sir Edmund Hillary credited him with.
questions.explain: Hillary said that when there seems no way out, you should pray for Shackleton, crediting his leadership with the crew's survival.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each view to who held it in the Tolstoys' marriage.
pairs: She could not see into his soul
She used him for fame and money
questions.explain: Each partner saw the other through divergent values and hardened into a defensive position, the mark of a narcissistic relationship.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each type in Chapter 2's examples to Greene's main advice about it.
pairs: Keep your distance before you are drawn in
See through the trick; the focus is always on them
Change the dynamic by entering the other's values
Model yourself on his mood reading
questions.explain: Three types are to be resisted or repaired; Shackleton's way of reading moods is the one Greene says should serve as a model.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Match each Chapter 2 example to the idea from the chapter's first half, The Narcissistic Spectrum, that it illustrates.
pairs: The narcissistic leader, the most dangerous deep narcissist
The deep narcissist who must keep attracting attention
Narcissism measured in relationships, not just people
The healthy narcissist turning outward to empathy
questions.explain: The second half puts the first half's spectrum into stories, from the toxic leader and attention-seeker to the healthy narcissist who develops empathy.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these behaviours of Joseph Stalin into his early charm and his later control.

items.t: Urging lieutenants to use the familiar form of address
Accessible even to junior officials
Singing and telling earthy jokes
Ending meetings on an intimate note
Firing his most experienced generals
Overseeing the size and shape of bayonets
Ordering lieutenants to dance at dinners
Listening eagerly to accounts of torture

questions.explain: Greene shows the congenial early Stalin slowly revealing another side as his power grew.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these items from the Loudun story into what Jeanne displayed and Greene's explanation of it.

items.t: Erotic dreams of Grandier
Names appearing on her palm
Fragrant oil from Saint Joseph
Demons refusing to leave her
A mix of fabrication and autosuggestion
Writing traced with acid, starch or a fingernail
Skill at concocting herbal remedies
Finding the loss of attention unbearable

questions.explain: For each apparent sign of possession or grace, Greene offers a mundane cause rooted in her appetite for attention.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these actions by whether Leo Tolstoy or Sonya did them.

items.t: Showed his diaries before the wedding
Wrote The Kreutzer Sonata
Vowed celibacy
Left home in the middle of the night
Copied out War and Peace
Walked out into the snow
Read the diaries on the sly
Tried to pit the children against the other

questions.explain: Each partner's actions provoked the other, the cycle Greene sees as a narcissistic dynamic.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these cues Shackleton monitored into those for reading individuals and those for reading the group.

items.t: Tone of voice
How quickly a man ate
How slowly a man rose from bed
Chattiness at mealtimes
Amount of swearing during work
How fast the mood lifted with entertainment

questions.explain: Greene says Shackleton divided his attention almost equally between individuals and the group.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these into what Shackleton did and what he avoided doing.

items.t: Hid his own doubts and fears
Let the men feel his optimism through his manner
Treated each man by his particular psychology
Scolding men whose spirits dipped
Discussing escape ideas the first morning
Singling out McNeish for stopping

questions.explain: Shackleton set the tone through his own attitude and lifted spirits indirectly, since scolding would shame people and spread negativity.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these signs into the complete control narcissist or the theatrical narcissist.

items.t: Attention followed by a coquettish pullback
Double binds where nothing pleases them
Turning against former friends
Always superior in goodness or suffering
Everything done for public consumption
Reveling in status as a victim

questions.explain: The first type works through control of emotions; the second through drama that keeps the focus on them.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Sort these topics into the half of Chapter 2 where they appear.

items.t: Defining the functional narcissist
The four components of the empathic skill set
The attribution bias
Stalin's late-night dinners
The possessions at Loudun
Shackleton on the ice floe

questions.explain: The first half sets out the spectrum and the empathic skills; the second half shows them through four historical cases.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: In the Stalin example, why did Sergey Kirov's loyalty in revealing the 1934 plot end up endangering him?
questions.a: By reporting the plot, Kirov showed Stalin that he was not as popular as he thought and that one person in particular was more liked than him. Stalin's manner turned cold, and Kirov's efforts to soothe him with lavish praise only made Stalin more suspicious. His old jokes at Stalin's expense now looked different, and he was assassinated in December 1934.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How did Stalin's apparent modesty coexist with the cult that grew around him?
questions.a: Outwardly he played the modest proletarian and reacted angrily to suggestions of public tribute. Yet his name and image appeared everywhere, Pravda almost deified him, and planes spelled his name at parades. He denied involvement but did nothing to stop it, and spoke of himself in the third person as an infallible revolutionary force.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Explain the double bind Stalin created for his generals and what it led to.
questions.a: If the generals spoke their minds, Stalin could be deeply insulted; if they deferred, he raged at their yes-saying. Feeling alone in the war effort, he fired his most competent generals and oversaw every detail himself, down to bayonets. Reading his moods became a matter of life or death for those around him.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, how are complete control narcissists able to charm and mesmerize people despite being so self-obsessed?
questions.a: They have more ambition and deeper insecurities than most deep narcissists, and their hypersensitivity to slights gives them fine antennae for others' desires and insecurities. They can listen with deep attention and mimic empathy, but they do it to control rather than connect. Their attention followed by coldness works like the push and pull of the coquette, and with their high confidence it attracts followers.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why, according to Greene, do complete control narcissists end up destroying themselves?
questions.a: As they grow secure in power they resent having played the charm game and turn on former friends, ruling by double binds and terror. People become automatons, so they must micromanage everything. But it is impossible to rid the human animal of free will, and people eventually rebel, as Stalin's lieutenants did by leaving him to die after his stroke.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why does Greene say the danger from a complete control narcissist lies at the beginning, and how should you protect yourself?
questions.a: The danger is when they first apply their charm, because once you are close you cannot get away. Use visceral empathy to sense that their interest is shallow and followed by a coquettish pullback, and look at their past for the lack of any intimate relationship and signs of a troubled childhood. Listen to people who warn you, notice the fear of those who serve them, and keep your distance.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How did Jeanne de Belciel change her method of getting attention when she moved to Loudun?
questions.a: At Poitiers her sarcasm and air of superiority had driven the nuns mad. At Loudun she instead set out to excel everyone in spiritual knowledge and piety, making a complete show of both. This won the prioress's favour and made Jeanne head of the house at twenty-five.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Why did Jeanne cling to her demons after Grandier's execution, and how did she use Father Surin?
questions.a: The other nuns felt guilt at their part in an innocent man's death, but Jeanne felt only the sudden loss of attention as unbearable, so she upped the ante. She had become a master at sensing the weaknesses and hidden desires of those around her. Surin wanted so badly to be the one to redeem her that he fell for simple miracles such as the stigmata and the fragrant oil.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: Using the Theatrical Narcissist example, explain Greene's paradox that deep narcissism often goes unnoticed.
questions.a: Deep narcissists sense early that showing their need for constant attention and superiority would repel people, so they become masters of disguise. Lacking a coherent self, they can play many parts, appearing more moral and altruistic than anyone or reveling in victimhood. People get caught up in the drama and only later find themselves consumed by the narcissist's needs.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How does Greene say you can recognize a theatrical narcissist?
questions.a: The focus always seems to be on them, and they are always superior in supposed goodness, suffering or squalor. Notice the continual drama and the theatrical quality of their gestures, since everything they do or say is for public consumption. The solution is to see through the trick and not become collateral damage in their drama.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: How did the episode of Tolstoy's diaries set the pattern for his marriage to Sonya?
questions.a: Tolstoy meant the diaries as honesty, a sign he was leaving his old ways for a new life with her. Sonya, from a conventional household, read them as proof he regretted his proposal, while Tolstoy took her reaction to mean she could not see into his soul. Each misunderstood the other and fell into hardened positions that lasted forty-eight years.

questions.unitTitle: Transform Self-love into Empathy
questions.q: According to Greene, what could Tolstoy and Sonya each have done differently during his spiritual crisis?
questions.a: Tolstoy could have foreseen that Sonya, never deeply spiritual and used to comfort, would resist, and explained his own side without demanding she follow him.
