questions.explain: Greene concludes that the ability to play many roles and blend masculine and feminine was the source of her power, and she lost it only when she narrowed herself for Feo.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what went wrong for Caterina Sforza in her marriage to Giacomo Feo?
questions.a: Worn down by an abusive husband, many pregnancies and fragile alliances, she sought respite by giving up power for love. In narrowing herself to the role of devoted wife she repressed her naturally expansive character and spent her energy placating Feo’s insecurities. She lost all initiative and paid with a depression that nearly killed her, a lesson after which she stayed true to herself.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Isabella d’Este, ruler of ____, found Caterina Sforza inspiring and praised the daring and valor of the Italian woman.
questions.explain: Greene uses Isabella d’Este, a contemporary ruler of Mantua, to show that women admired Caterina’s strength.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why, according to Greene, were men so drawn to Caterina Sforza?
questions.a: Men could talk battle and strategy with her as with an equal, unlike the other women in their lives. More importantly, they sensed a freedom in her: they too had to play a constricting role, always in control, tough and indomitable, and secretly they were drawn to a dangerous woman with whom they could lose control. Her unrepressed authenticity made them want to let go as well.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says the world of Caterina Sforza is too distant from ours for her story to tell us much about gender roles today.
questions.explain: He warns that thinking so would be a great mistake: the details of gender roles change with culture and period, but the pattern is essentially the same.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these natural qualities does Greene say children show before gender roles trim them away?
options: Girls have an adventurous and exploratory spirit
Girls are naturally more deferential than boys
Boys are naturally less sensitive than girls
Boys have high degrees of empathy and sensitivity
Boys are at an early age more emotionally reactive than girls
questions.explain: Greene says young boys are emotionally reactive, empathetic and sensitive, while girls are adventurous with powerful wills. Deference is something girls are later pressured into, not a natural trait.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the pattern Greene says holds across cultures for gender roles in order.
items: We are born complete beings with many sides
We must present a consistent identity to the world
We trim and lop off natural qualities
We become less dimensional and conform to expected roles
We feel fascination with those who are less repressed
questions.explain: Greene traces our development from completeness to conformity, noting that we often realize what we have lost only when we meet someone less repressed.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these into what boys and what girls are pressured to give up, according to Greene.

items.t: A rich range of emotions
Natural empathy, in the struggle to get ahead
Sensitivity
Their assertive sides
Putting their own feelings first
Being aggressive, even as a boss

questions.explain: Boys repress emotion and empathy to get ahead; girls must be nice, deferential and never too aggressive, always putting others’ feelings before their own.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these men does Greene name as displaying an unmistakable feminine undertone that intrigued people?
options: Duke Ellington
Benjamin Disraeli
Richard Nixon
Cesare Borgia
David Bowie
questions.explain: Greene lists Disraeli, Duke Ellington, John F. Kennedy and David Bowie as male counterparts to Caterina. Nixon appears later as a hypermasculine type, and Borgia as her enemy.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says power lies in exploring that middle ____ between the masculine and the feminine, in playing against people’s expectations.
questions.explain: Rather than overidentifying with one pole, he urges exploring the middle range and expanding the roles you play.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A manager who always defends her team’s plans when challenged decides, next time, to raise sharp questions about her critic’s own plan. Which advice from Greene does she follow?
options: Play the expected gender role more convincingly
Respond to resistance in different ways, attacking when you normally defend
Withdraw your projections from your critics
Blend the analytical with the intuitive
questions.explain: Greene advises training yourself to respond to problems and resistance differently, attacking when you normally defend or vice versa, to expand your repertoire.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What practical steps does Greene suggest for letting go of rigid overidentification with your gender role?
questions.a: Return to the harder or softer sides you have repressed: develop greater empathy, or learn to be less deferential. Respond to resistance in new ways, attacking when you normally defend or the reverse, and blend the analytical with the intuitive to become more creative. Don’t worry about people’s reactions; being hard to categorize will fascinate them.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What does the Proust epigraph at the end of the Authentic Gender section say love engages us with at first?
options: A doll fashioned in our own brain
The real woman of the external world
A mirror of our own parents
A rival we wish to defeat
questions.explain: Proust calls it the deception of love that it starts with play not with a real woman but with a doll fashioned in our brain, introducing the idea of projection in the Keys section.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the events of the 1488 Ravaldino crisis in Caterina Sforza’s story in order.
items: Conspirators stab Girolamo and capture Caterina
Caterina begs Tommaso Feo to surrender, but he refuses
Feo demands she enter alone to sign a letter
Inside, she is held as a hostage by Feo
Conspirators threaten her children below the ramparts
A Milanese army arrives and the assassins scatter
questions.explain: The staged negotiation got Caterina inside the fortress; the threat to her children came the next day, and she held out until the Milanese army arrived ten days later.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the events of Cesare Borgia’s campaign against Caterina Sforza in order.
items: Borgia takes Imola and enters Forlì
Borgia rides up to Ravaldino on December 26
The drawbridge trick fails
Cannon fire opens a breach in the walls
A soldier betrays Caterina for the reward
She is imprisoned in the Castel Sant’Angelo
questions.explain: Greene narrates the siege from the fall of Imola and Forlì, through the failed trick and the breach, to her betrayal and year in prison.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the steps of Greene’s Interpretation of Caterina Sforza’s story in order.
items: Women’s roles were severely restricted
Her unique upbringing let her develop in any direction
She could play many roles, blending masculine and feminine
She lost this only when she narrowed herself for Feo
She fascinated the men and women of her time
questions.explain: The Interpretation moves from the restricted circle, to her exceptional education, to the blend that was her power, its one lapse, and finally its effect on others.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each place to what happened there in Caterina Sforza’s story.
pairs: Castle in Milan where she was raised
Where she learned to hunt boars and stags
Castle she seized to control Rome, and later her prison
Fortress of Forlì she defended against assassins and Borgia
questions.explain: These places frame her life: a free upbringing in Milan, physical training in the hunt, and the two castles where she showed, and finally lost, her power.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each of Caterina Sforza’s husbands to Greene’s description of him.
pairs: Papal nephew, a moody hothead paralyzed by fear
Former stable boy who worshipped her but was insecure
Florentine who, more than anyone, reminded her of her father
questions.explain: Greene contrasts the weak Girolamo, the adoring but insecure Feo, and Medici, her equal in knowledge, power and refinement, who died the year they married.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these behaviors of Caterina Sforza into times she stayed true to her expansive character and the period she narrowed herself for Giacomo Feo.

items.t: Seizing the Castel Sant’Angelo
Staging the hostage drama with Tommaso Feo
Fighting on the front line against Borgia
Retiring from public affairs
Handing her governing powers to her husband
Spending her energy placating his insecurities

questions.explain: Greene says her power came from playing many roles; with Feo she shrank to the devoted wife, lost all initiative and fell into depression.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, why did Caterina Sforza fall so completely for Giacomo Feo?
options: She needed his family’s armies to defend Forlì
He reminded her of her father’s strength and learning
Worn down by immense pressures, she sought respite by giving up power for love
She was forced into the match by the new pope
questions.explain: Greene says that after an abusive husband, many pregnancies and fragile alliances, it was natural to seek respite in his adoring attention. It was Medici, not Feo, who reminded her of her father.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, in what aspect of life are our beliefs that we are consistent, mature and in control most easily shattered?
options: When we face a career failure
When we are in a crowd
When we fall in love
When we confront death
questions.explain: Greene says these self-opinions are easily shattered when we fall in love, becoming prey to emotions we cannot control and making choices we cannot explain.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene suggests that when we fall in love, we are actually being more ourselves, because the mask of reasonableness slips off.
questions.explain: He asks us to consider that in daily life we are sleepwalking behind a mask; in love the mask slips and unconscious forces show.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene suggests that in our conscious day-to-day life we are ____, unaware of who we really are and mistaking the mask for reality.
questions.explain: He reverses the usual view that love is temporary madness: it is ordinary life that is the sleepwalk.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these changes does Greene say commonly occur when we are in love?
options: Our attention becomes obsessively absorbed in one person
We regress to childish behavior and fear abandonment
Our moods become steadier and calmer
We judge people’s character more accurately than usual
Traits opposite to our usual ones come to the fore
questions.explain: Greene lists obsession, opposite traits, childish regression, terror of abandonment and wild mood swings. Our judgment of character gets worse, not better.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each type to the flattering quality Greene says we mistake it for when infatuated.
questions.explain: Greene uses these pairs to show how love warps our normally decent judgment of character, and how we repeat the same misjudgments.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In Greene’s account of falling in love, what is person B?
options: The partner we project our fantasies onto
The irrational self that emerges and dominates as infatuation deepens
A rival who threatens the relationship
The rational self we show the world
questions.explain: Person A is our normal rational self; person B is the immature, irrational self that takes over as we fall in love, which Jung called the anima or animus.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: How does Greene describe the behavior of person B, the self that takes over when we are deeply in love?
questions.a: Person B sees qualities in people that are not there and acts in counterproductive, even self-destructive ways. It is immature, with unrealistic expectations, and makes decisions that later seem mysterious to rational person A. The deeper we fall in love, the more B dominates.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Carl Jung called the unconscious feminine part of the boy and man the ____.
questions.explain: Jung named the possessing entity anima for the male and animus for the female; both surface when someone of the opposite sex fascinates us.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these does Greene give as origins of the anima and animus?
options: Hormones and genes of the opposite sex within us
The shadow side of that parent, which the child must deal with
The friends we make in adolescence
The influence of the parent of the opposite sex
The first person we fall in love with
questions.explain: Greene traces the anima and animus to our contrasexual traits and to what we absorb, good and bad, from the opposite-sex parent. Later loves trigger them but do not create them.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why, according to Greene, does the parent of the opposite sex shape our personality so deeply?
questions.a: In our earliest years we are completely open, and the opposite-sex parent is our first encounter with someone dramatically different from us. Relating to their alien nature makes our personality more dimensional and multifaceted, whereas with the same-sex parent there is comfort and immediate identification. We absorb their positive and negative qualities unconsciously, charged with intense emotions.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these traits into those Greene says small boys often learn from the mother and small girls from the father.

items.t: Overt affection
Empathy
Sensitivity
Aggression
Boldness
Intellectual rigor
Physical prowess

questions.explain: Greene says small children are comfortable expressing these traits absorbed from the opposite-sex parent before gender identity pushes them underground.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what is the simplest and most powerful way for a child to forge an identity separate from the parents?
options: Choosing friends the parents disapprove of
Imitating the parent of the same sex exactly
Building it around gender roles, the masculine and the feminine
Excelling at school and in a career
questions.explain: Greene says that in the critical period of separation, the simplest and most powerful way to create identity is around gender roles.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Describe the boy’s ambivalent relationship to his mother, as Greene presents it, and what it leads him to repress.
questions.a: He craves the security and adoring attention she gives him, yet feels threatened by her, as if she might suffocate him in her femininity, and he fears her power over his life. To differentiate himself he overidentifies with the masculine role, playing up toughness and independence. His empathy, gentleness and need for connection sink into the unconscious.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what do the cultural expectations on a girl turn into?
options: Voices in her head that judge her and make her doubt her self-worth
An identification with her father’s ambitions
A rebellious streak she expresses openly
A strong sense of her own assertiveness
questions.explain: Expectations to be nice, sweet and deferential become internal voices continually judging her, and her exploratory, aggressive sides sink into the unconscious.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these sides of a girl’s character does Greene say tend to be repressed if she adopts a more traditionally feminine role?
options: Her wish to please others
Her exploratory side
Her concern with looking pretty
Her aggressive side
Her darker side
questions.explain: Greene says the exploratory, aggressive and darker sides, natural or absorbed from the father, sink into the unconscious; pleasing others and looking pretty are what the role demands.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, the person who draws our attention romantically most often bears some resemblance to whom?
options: Our ideal self
Our first teacher
Our closest childhood friend
Our mother or father
questions.explain: Greene says the person who attracts us unconsciously resembles, physically or psychologically, our mother or father, reviving that charged primal relationship.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each kind of relationship with the opposite-sex parent to the projection Greene says it tends to produce.
pairs: Projecting the parent’s desirable qualities to relive an early paradise
Choosing someone like the imperfect parent to fix the original bond
Seeking someone with opposite, often darker qualities
questions.explain: Greene distinguishes three patterns of projection depending on whether the early relationship was positive, inconsistent or negative.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A young woman raised by a strict, distant, critical father keeps falling for unconventional rebels. How does Greene explain this?
options: She is reliving the comfort of her father’s protection
She is projecting her mother’s nurturing qualities
The rebel is her animus, the wild side she never dared express
She is trying to fix her father’s inconsistent attention
questions.explain: Greene uses this very pattern: after a negative relationship she seeks the father’s opposite, and the rebel is her animus externalized.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why, according to Greene, do relationships built on anima or animus projections tend to fall apart, and repeat?
questions.a: Because we are relating not to the person as they are but to our projections, we eventually feel disappointed and blame them for not being what we imagined. Misreadings and miscommunications on both sides break the relationship. Unaware of the source, we go through precisely the same cycle with the next person.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene gives the composer Frédéric Chopin and the writer George ____ as a famous successful contrasexual couple.
questions.explain: In this couple Sand was more like the husband and Chopin like the wife, an example of a psychologically feminine man drawn to a masculine woman.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says contrasexual couples, in which the man is more feminine and the woman more masculine, are always doomed to fail.
questions.explain: He says they can be successful if both sides get what they want, citing Chopin and George Sand.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the three tasks Greene sets for the student of human nature in his order.
items: Observe the anima and animus in others
Become aware of the projecting mechanism in yourself
Look inward at your own repressed qualities and integrate them
questions.explain: Greene moves from observing others, to catching your own projections, to inner integration, ending with how this eases the conflict between the sexes.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why does Greene advise observing people’s anima or animus in their intimate relationships?
questions.a: Their behavior and patterns in intimate relationships give you access to their unconscious, which is normally hidden from you. You can see the parts of themselves they have repressed and use that knowledge to great effect. Hypermasculine and hyperfeminine people deserve special attention, because their repressed side lurks just below the surface.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says that when people go extra far in repressing their feminine or masculine qualities, these leak out in a ____ form.
questions.explain: The hypermasculine man and the hyperfeminine woman show their repressed side in exaggerated, distorted ways.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these leaks into those Greene associates with the hypermasculine man and with the hyperfeminine woman.

items.t: Secret obsession with clothes and looks
Snippy judgments of other men’s appearance
Tantrums when his uninformed opinions are challenged
Sudden sentimentality
Seductive, girlish teasing as a ploy for power
Passive-aggressive domination
Irrational stubbornness in petty matters

questions.explain: The repressed feminine leaks out of the hypermasculine man as fussiness and emotion; the repressed masculine leaks out of the hyperfeminine woman as hidden anger and underhanded willfulness.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which US president does Greene cite as projecting a macho image while fussing over the color of suits and office drapes?
options: Richard Nixon
Ronald Reagan
Lyndon Johnson
John F. Kennedy
questions.explain: Greene uses Nixon as the hypermasculine man whose repressed feminine side leaked out in fussing over suits and drapes. Kennedy is named earlier for an appealing feminine undertone.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says you should try to stop projecting onto people of the opposite sex altogether.
questions.explain: He says projections have a positive role and could not be stopped anyway; without them you would not become fascinated and fall in love. The task is to withdraw them as the relationship develops.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What does Greene mean by withdrawing your projections, and what does it make possible?
questions.a: Once a relationship develops, you need the awareness to take back the qualities you projected so you can see the person as they really are. You may find you are incompatible, or the opposite. If you stay, you can still idealize them, but on the basis of their actual positive qualities, perhaps even finding their faults charming.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A man feels unusually stung when a female colleague postpones a meeting he requested, though he would shrug it off from a male colleague. How does Greene explain this?
options: He is reacting to her passive-aggressive manner
He is simply under heavy pressure at work
He is envious of her higher status
Projections and emotions are stirred more strongly by people of the opposite sex
questions.explain: Greene uses this office example: when the person is of the opposite sex, resentments, fears and projections are stirred up that a same-sex colleague would not trigger.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene’s third task is to integrate repressed traits into your everyday personality, so that they no longer operate independently and automatically in the form of ____.
questions.explain: Integrated, the anima or animus becomes part of your everyday self rather than a person B that possesses you, and people sense your authenticity.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says that the assertiveness you desire to see in a man, or the empathy you desire in a woman, is a sign of what?
options: A quality you need to develop within yourself
A sign that you have found the right partner
A trait your parent failed to model for you
A quality you should demand from your partner
questions.explain: Glimpses of your anima or animus appear in what you seek from the opposite sex; the third task is to develop that undertone in yourself.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene argues that we are on a continual line of progress toward perfect equality between the sexes and are close to reaching it.
questions.explain: He says we like to imagine this, but on a deeper level there is increasing tension and polarization between the sexes.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, why is the hostility between the sexes stronger among men?
options: It may relate to latent hostility toward the mother figure and the dependency she triggers
Men have lost economic power to women
Men are taught to compete with every woman they meet
Men are naturally more aggressive than women
questions.explain: Greene ties it to latent hostility toward the mother figure and the dependency and weakness she triggers, giving masculinity a defensive, insecure edge.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: How does Greene connect the outer conflict between the sexes to an inner conflict, and what does he propose?
questions.a: He says the outer conflict between the genders is merely a reflection of an unresolved inner conflict: as long as the inner feminine or masculine is denied, the outer distance will grow. When we bridge that distance within, we relate to the opposite sex as to parts of ourselves. The inner connection improves the outer one, which should be the ideal we aim for.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these into what Greene associates with healthy polarity between the sexes and with polarization.

items.t: Still causes us to be attracted and fall in love
Includes a desire to get closer to the other
Relating to the other sex as parts of ourselves
The other sex seems like alien creatures
Distance turning into hostility
Pushing people further apart

questions.explain: Greene contrasts polarity, which keeps attraction alive while seeking closeness, with polarization, in which distance and hostility come to the fore.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each term from the Keys section of the Law of Gender Rigidity to its meaning.
pairs: Opposite-sex hormones and genes we all carry
The irrational self that emerges in love
Seeing our own buried qualities in another
questions.explain: These are the core terms Greene draws from Jung to explain why love possesses us and how to integrate what we repress.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the stages of the anima or animus cycle that Greene describes in order.
items: Qualities absorbed from the opposite-sex parent are repressed
Someone resembling that parent fascinates us
We project our buried qualities onto them
We are disappointed that they are not what we imagined
The relationship collapses and the cycle repeats
questions.explain: Greene traces how repressed contrasexual traits are triggered by a person resembling a parent, projected, then disappointed, leading to the same cycle with the next person.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the steps of a boy’s development in Greene’s account in order.
items: He absorbs affection and empathy from his mother
He feels threatened by her power and femininity
He needs to differentiate himself from her
He overidentifies with toughness and independence
His gentleness sinks into the unconscious as the anima
questions.explain: Greene describes the boy moving from closeness to the mother, through ambivalence and separation, to overidentification and repression of the feminine side.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says the trait that a man’s anima supplies is often one he never ____ in himself.
questions.explain: In the example of the adored son, the woman supplies him the qualities he never developed in himself, so he falls in love with his own anima.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A woman who prides herself on independence becomes needy and jealous once she falls for a new partner. How would Greene describe this?
options: She is finally seeing her partner as he really is
She is reacting to a narcissistic partner
Opposite traits come to the fore as person B emerges
She is consciously testing her partner’s loyalty
questions.explain: Greene says that in love a normally strong, independent person can become helpless and dependent, as the anima or animus, person B, takes over.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each figure Greene cites in Chapter 12 to the point the figure illustrates.
pairs: Explained love as possession by the anima or animus
Macho image with a repressed side that leaked out
A man whose feminine undertone intrigued people
A woman who admired Caterina’s strength
questions.explain: Greene draws on these figures to show possession in love, caricatured repression, contrasexual couples and the fascination of a blended character.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these into what Greene associates with person A and with person B in someone who is falling in love.

items.t: Presents a front of reasonableness
Feels consistent, mature and in control
Finds later decisions mysterious
Sees qualities that are not there
Acts in self-destructive ways
Has unrealistic, immature expectations

questions.explain: Person A is the rational everyday self; person B is the anima or animus that possesses us in love and whose choices later puzzle person A.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What does the subtitle The Law of Gender Rigidity signal about the problem Chapter 12 addresses?
options: Rigid rules are needed to keep relationships stable
Overidentifying with the expected gender role makes us rigid
Men and women are fundamentally unable to understand each other
Gender roles are fixed by biology and cannot change
questions.explain: The law diagnoses rigidity as the cost of overidentifying with a role; the chapter title gives the remedy, reconnecting to the masculine or feminine within.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why does Chapter 12 open with the story of Caterina Sforza before the Keys to Human Nature section?
questions.a: Her life dramatizes the chapter’s ideal: a woman whose unique upbringing let her blend feminine and masculine traits and play many roles, which was the source of her power and her fascination for others. Her one lapse, narrowing herself for Giacomo Feo, shows the cost of rigidity. The Keys section then explains the psychology, through Jung’s anima and animus, of why most of us lose that range.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: within Chapter 12, the Keys to Human Nature section points ahead to the following section for common types of projections.
questions.explain: In the second task Greene tells the reader to see the next section, Gender Projection—Types, for common types of projections.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which later section of Chapter 12 does Greene say will say more about blending the analytical with the intuitive?
options: The Original Man/Woman
The Authentic Gender
Keys to Human Nature
Gender Projection—Types
questions.explain: Greene twice refers readers to the final section of the chapter, The Original Man/Woman, for more on integration and blending modes of thinking.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the sections of Chapter 12 in order.
items: The Authentic Gender
Keys to Human Nature
Gender Projection—Types
The Original Man/Woman
questions.explain: The chapter moves from Caterina’s story, to the Jungian explanation, to types of projection, and ends with the integrated ideal.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these earlier laws share Chapter 12’s theme of parts of ourselves that are repressed and then leak out?
options: The Law of Role-playing (See Through People’s Masks)
The Law of Covetousness (Become an Elusive Object of Desire)
The Law of Repression (Confront Your Dark Side)
The Law of Envy (Beware the Fragile Ego)
questions.explain: Like the shadow in Chapter 9, the anima and animus are repressed and leak out in caricature; and Chapter 12’s idea that our reasonable front is a mask that slips in love echoes Chapter 3’s masks.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: How does Chapter 12’s Keys section echo the theme of Chapter 1, Master Your Emotional Self?
questions.a: Chapter 1 deals with the Law of Irrationality. Chapter 12 shows that falling in love exposes the essential irrationality in our nature: person B takes over, unconscious forces drive our choices, and our rational self, person A, cannot explain them. Both chapters ask us to become aware of these forces rather than imagine we are in control.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each chapter to its law.
pairs: Chapter 12, Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
Chapter 13, Advance with a Sense of Purpose
questions.explain: Chapter 12 sits between grandiosity and aimlessness, and links back to the repression of Chapter 9.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the title Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You, what does the word reconnect imply?
options: The traits belong only to people in love
The traits are new skills to be acquired in adulthood
The traits must be learned from the opposite sex
The traits were ours originally and were lost or repressed
questions.explain: Greene argues we are born complete, with qualities of both sexes, and lose them in forming a consistent identity; so the task is to reconnect, not to acquire.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, besides recognizing gender projection in yourself and using it to see into other people's unconscious, what is the third way Greene says to use knowledge of the projection types?
options: Be attentive to how others project their needs and fantasies onto you
Encourage partners to project onto you so you can control them
Choose partners whose projections match your own childhood
Teach your children to avoid forming any projections at all
questions.explain: Greene's third use is watching how others project their needs and fantasies onto you, since being the target of a projection has its own dangers.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, why does Greene warn against becoming the target of other people's gender projections?
questions.a: When others project onto us, we are tempted to live up to their idealization and believe we are as great, strong or empathetic as they imagine. Without realizing it we start playing the role they want, becoming the mother or father figure they crave. Inevitably we come to resent this, because we cannot be ourselves and are not appreciated for our true qualities.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: in the Devilish Romantic projection, the man who fascinates the woman is often older and successful.
questions.explain: Greene describes him as often older and successful, a rake who chases young women but who is also romantic when in love.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Devilish Romantic gender projection, what kind of early relationship does the woman usually have had with her father?
options: A rather intense, even flirtatious relationship in which he turned to her for inspiration
A distant, strict relationship in which he criticized her constantly
A formal relationship in which he pushed her to excel at school
Almost no relationship, because he left the family early
questions.explain: Such fathers often find their wives boring and the daughter more charming, and she becomes addicted to his attention. The strict, critical father belongs to the Lovable Rebel projection instead.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, how does a father's attention create the Devilish Romantic projection in a daughter?
questions.a: A father who finds his wife boring turns to his young daughter for inspiration, and she becomes addicted to his attention and adept at playing the kind of girl daddy wants, which gives her a sense of power. Recapturing that attention becomes her lifelong goal. Any association with the father figure sparks the projection, and she invents or exaggerates a man's romantic nature.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, how does Greene describe Jack Bouvier, the father of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis?
options: A shy scholar who doted on her education
A distant businessman she rarely saw after the divorce
A stern patriarch who disapproved of her suitors
A handsome narcissist and womanizer who treated her more like a playmate than a daughter
questions.explain: Greene calls him a dashing narcissist, a notorious womanizer who treated Jackie more like a playmate and lover than a daughter; she kept spending time with him even after the divorce.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put these stages of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis's life, as Greene tells it, in order.
items: She is her father’s favorite and takes his side in her parents’ fights
As a young woman she turns her attention to older, powerful, unconventional men
She marries John F. Kennedy, who is too self-absorbed to give her attention
She marries Aristotle Onassis, who treats her horribly and cheats on her
questions.explain: Greene traces the pattern from her bond with Jack Bouvier through her choice of men to two marriages that repeated the same disappointment.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says Jacqueline Kennedy found in John F. Kennedy the attentive, romantic husband she had been seeking.
questions.explain: Kennedy was closest to her ideal in looks and spirit, but he was too self-absorbed and busy with affairs to give her the attention she craved; he was not really the romantic type.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Devilish Romantic projection, why would the woman not be satisfied even by a completely attentive and tirelessly romantic man?
questions.a: She is searching for a man who does not exist. A man who was completely attentive and tirelessly romantic would bore her and seem too weak. She is secretly drawn to the devilish side of her fantasy man and to the narcissism that comes with it.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what is the only way out of the Devilish Romantic trap?
options: See the pattern, stop mythologizing the father, and focus on the damage his attention caused
Become as cold and self-absorbed as the men she chooses
Avoid all older and successful men for the rest of her life
Find a man who is truly as romantic as the father seemed
questions.explain: Greene says such women must see the pattern itself, stop mythologizing the father, and focus on the harm done by his inappropriate attention.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection, what do you notice when such a man talks about his perfect woman?
options: There is not a lot of concrete detail about what makes her so perfect
He compares her mainly to his father
He lists her flaws in great detail
He speaks of her only in terms of her social status
questions.explain: His fantasy is vague because he cannot verbalize what he missed; he has had few real encounters with her and imagines the rest.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says the woman who triggers the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection often conforms to what Freud called the ____ woman, self-contained and not needing anyone to complete her.
questions.explain: Freud's narcissistic woman is cold at the core and a blank screen onto which men project whatever they want.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: For men prone to the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection, the woman serves as a ____, a great spark to their imagination.
questions.explain: She is a lure to loosen up their rigid minds; Greene says they must learn to find this inspiration within themselves.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection, what kind of mother does the man usually have had?
options: A mother who adored him and filled him with confidence
A strong mother who made him an obedient, studious boy
A mother who was not totally there and expected the son to give her attention and validation
A mother who was flirtatious and treated him like a playmate
questions.explain: Because of this reversal, the man feels a great emptiness he constantly needs to fill. The adoring mother belongs to the Woman to Worship Him projection, and the strong mother to the Fallen Woman.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why is the Elusive Woman of Perfection fantasy so vague, and why does the man keep moving on to the next woman?
questions.a: His mother was not totally there for him and expected him to give her the validation she lacked, leaving him with a great emptiness he cannot exactly name. Since he cannot verbalize what he missed, his fantasy has little concrete detail. When a real relationship forms he becomes disenchanted, decides she misled him, and projects the fantasy onto the next woman; it is always the next one who will be perfect.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says men with the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection often prefer chasing their fantasy because in that scenario they are in control and free to leave.
questions.explain: Greene says they prefer the chase because they stay in control and have the freedom to leave when reality sets in; breaking the pattern means giving up some of that control.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What must a man with the Elusive Woman of Perfection projection do to break his pattern?
questions.a: He must recognize the pattern, find and interact with a real woman, accept her inevitable flaws and give more of himself, giving up some of his control. Rather than needing a muse, he must find inspiration within by bringing out more of his own anima and loosening his thinking. Not needing wildness from a fantasy woman, he will relate better to actual women.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Lovable Rebel projection, what does the woman discover once a relationship actually forms?
options: He is a genuine rebel who is too free to settle down
He is gentle and passive, nothing like his appearance
He is secretly wealthy and well connected
He is lazy and ineffectual, and quite conventional, controlling and domineering
questions.explain: Despite the tattoos and shaved head, he cannot hold down a job because he is lazy, not because he is a rebel, and he is controlling and domineering.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says that, unlike the Devilish Romantic, the Lovable Rebel is usually an older and highly successful man.
questions.explain: It is the reverse: the Lovable Rebel is often young and not so successful, and usually outside her usual circle, which makes the relationship slightly taboo.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what kind of father does a woman with the Lovable Rebel projection usually have?
options: A rebellious father who was often in trouble with the law
A strong, patriarchal father who was distant, strict and critical
A playful father who doted on her and neglected her mother
A weak father who let her mother make all the decisions
questions.explain: The father represents order, rules and conventions; she internalized his critical voice and repressed her own desire to rebel.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Lovable Rebel projection, the woman's repressed desire to rebel goes into her animus, which is quite angry and ____.
questions.explain: Instead of developing rebelliousness herself she externalizes it onto a rebellious male, and her angry side emerges as she grows disenchanted.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, how does the Lovable Rebel projection arise, and what is Greene's remedy?
questions.a: A strict, critical patriarchal father left the daughter dreaming of rebellion but reduced to obeying, so her desire to rebel was repressed into an angry animus. Instead of developing it herself, she looks for it in a rebellious, often younger, man. The remedy is to accept that what she really wants is independence, assertiveness and the power to disobey in herself, built up in small everyday steps such as practicing saying no and breaking some rules.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these traits of the Lovable Rebel into how the woman imagines him and what she finds in a relationship.

items.t: A noticeable disdain for authority
A nonconformist
Slightly taboo, outside her usual circle
Lazy and ineffectual
Quite conventional underneath
Controlling and domineering

questions.explain: Greene contrasts the rebellious image that sparks her charged fantasies with the conventional, domineering man she discovers.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A woman raised by a stern, critical father keeps falling for young tattooed men who scorn rules, but each one turns out to be bossy and lazy. What does Greene advise her?
options: Avoid relationships until her father's voice fades on its own
Return to men her father would have approved of
Look for an older, more successful version of the same type
Develop independence and the power to disobey in herself, in small steps
questions.explain: This is the Lovable Rebel projection; what she really wants is to develop assertiveness herself, practicing it in everyday challenges.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In Proust's Swann's Way, what turns Charles Swann's curiosity about Odette into idealization?
options: Reading letters she had written to another lover
Deciding she resembles a woman in a reproduction of a Botticelli fresco
Learning that she came from an old noble family
Hearing her sing at a society party
questions.explain: Staring at a reproduction of a Botticelli biblical scene, he decides she resembles a woman in it, a highbrow reference with no relation to reality.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene describes Charles Swann, before meeting Odette, as a man eager to commit to a serious relationship.
questions.explain: Swann is an aesthete and a Don Juan who is deathly afraid of any relationship or commitment, yet he decides to marry Odette and educate her.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these descriptions of Odette in Swann's Way into how Swann imagines her and how she really is.

items.t: Has had a hard life and deserves better
Needs to be educated in the finer things
Resembles a woman in a Botticelli fresco
Extremely clever and strong willed
Much stronger than Swann is
Has affairs with other men and women
Makes him her passive slave

questions.explain: Swann projects weakness and a need for rescue onto Odette, but she proves the stronger of the two and dominates him.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene calls the Fallen Woman projection the classic split of the ____, wanting one type as a wife but feeling a stronger attraction to the other.
questions.explain: Such men want a mother figure for a wife but are physically drawn to the Fallen Woman type, the opposite of their good, civilized selves.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, why are men with strong mothers drawn to the Fallen Woman?
questions.a: Having strong mother figures, they became good, obedient boys and excellent students, repressing the playful, sensual and earthy sides they had as boys. They are too rigid and civilized, so they can only relate to these qualities through women who seem opposite to themselves. They tell themselves they want to protect such women, but what really attracts them is the danger and naughty pleasures these women seem to promise.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says the anima of men caught in the Fallen Woman projection is passive and ____.
questions.explain: Underestimating the strength of such women, these men often end up as their pawns, as Swann became Odette's passive slave.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these does Greene advise men with the Fallen Woman projection to do?
options: Develop the more physical and sensual side of their character
Commit firmly to a well-educated woman of their own class
Take more risks at work
Focus on rescuing a woman who needs their protection
Move outside their comfort zone and try new experiences on their own
questions.explain: Greene says such men need challenges, a bit of danger and a more sensual side so they can actively initiate the pleasures they crave. Marrying within their class or rescuing a woman repeats the split rather than healing it.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In George Eliot's Middlemarch, as Greene retells it, what does Dorothea Brooke discover after marrying Edward Causabon?
options: He has spent all his money and needs her inheritance
He is a brilliant scholar who resents her intelligence
He is dead inside, very controlling, and sees her as a glorified secretary
He is kind but too ill to finish his great work
questions.explain: Dorothea expected a spiritual genius who would educate and elevate her; instead she was trapped in a loveless marriage.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: In Greene's retelling of Middlemarch, Dorothea's sister and uncle were horrified by her interest in Causabon.
questions.explain: To them he was ugly, with moles and a sallow complexion, slurping his food and talking little, while Dorothea saw a spiritual quality in his face.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In Middlemarch, Dorothea dreams of helping Causabon complete his great masterpiece, The Key to All ____.
questions.explain: She imagines learning Greek and Latin to help him, as if marrying Pascal or Kant, an illustration of the Superior Man projection.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the stages of Dorothea Brooke's story in Middlemarch, as Greene tells it, in order.
items: She is courted by the young Sir James Chettam
She meets the much older scholar Edward Causabon
She sees spiritual depth where her family sees ugliness
She marries him to help with his great masterpiece
She finds he is dead inside and is trapped in a loveless marriage
questions.explain: The story moves from a suitable young suitor, to fascination with Causabon, to idealization, marriage and disillusionment.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these descriptions of Edward Causabon into how Dorothea sees him before marriage and what she discovers after.

items.t: His face is full of a spiritual quality
He is too above people to care about etiquette
He talks little because no one would understand him
Like being married to Pascal or Kant
Dead inside
Very controlling
Sees her as a glorified secretary

questions.explain: Dorothea reinterprets every flaw as a sign of genius, the hallmark of the Superior Man projection.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, what is the source of the Superior Man projection in women?
options: A father who adored her and treated her as a playmate
Boredom with men of her own age and class
Feelings of inferiority from internalizing the critical voices of the father and others
An inborn attraction to older, wealthy men
questions.explain: Never having developed her own strength, she searches for it in men and exaggerates any traces of it; her insecurity is acquired, not inherent.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What does Greene say a woman with the Superior Man projection must do to break free of it?
questions.a: She must first realize that her insecurity comes from the critical opinions of others that she has internalized, not from any inherent lack of intelligence or worth. Then she must build assertiveness and self-confidence through action, such as taking on projects, starting a business or mastering a craft. Seeing herself as men's natural equal, she can gauge the true worth and character of the men she meets.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these does Greene suggest for building the self-confidence of a woman with the Superior Man projection?
options: Finding an older mentor to guide her choices
Deferring to men until her confidence returns
Taking on projects
Mastering a craft
Starting a business
questions.explain: Greene says confidence must come through her own actions; looking to a superior man for guidance is exactly the projection she must escape.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A young graduate student is drawn to her famous professor, who seems brilliant and assured, though friends find him cold and self-important. Which projection does Greene's chapter say this fits?
options: The Superior Man
The Elusive Woman of Perfection
The Devilish Romantic
The Lovable Rebel
questions.explain: Greene calls the professor seducing the student the classic Superior Man case: the man is drawn to the adoring attention of a younger woman he can control.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Woman to Worship Him projection, why does the man eventually feel betrayed?
options: She stops being soothing and admiring once she resents the mother role he pushed her into
She reveals she never found him attractive
She leaves him for a more successful rival
She turns out to be far more ambitious than he is
questions.explain: He blames her for changing, but he projected qualities that were never exactly there and pushed her to conform to them.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the stages of the Woman to Worship Him projection in the order Greene describes them.
items: A driven man feels the world is harsh and something is missing
A warm, attentive woman who seems to admire him appears
He subtly positions her to play the mother role
She comes to resent the role and stops admiring him
He blames her for changing and feels betrayed
questions.explain: Greene traces the pattern from his need for comfort, through the role he forces on her, to her resentment and his sense of betrayal.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says the anima of the man with the Woman to Worship Him projection has a sharp, ____ edge, always ready to complain and blame.
questions.explain: His dependency on the mothering woman breeds resentment, and he may sabotage or withdraw from the relationship.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Woman to Worship Him projection, why is the breakup so painful for the man, and what must he develop?
questions.a: He has invested energy in this pattern since his earliest years, so losing the woman feels like abandonment by the mother figure. He must see that his ambition stems from wanting to please his mother and develop from within the mothering qualities he projects onto women. By learning to comfort and soothe himself and be satisfied with his accomplishments, he will give more and relate to women as they are.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these does Greene advise a man caught in the Woman to Worship Him projection to do?
options: Find a woman who is more naturally devoted and attentive
See his ambition as stemming from his desire to please his mother
Push himself harder so women will admire him again
Learn to comfort and soothe himself
Withdraw from time to time and be satisfied with his accomplishments
questions.explain: The cure is to develop mothering qualities within. Seeking a more devoted woman or striving harder for admiration only feeds the projection.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each gender projection type to the childhood relationship Greene traces it to.
pairs: An intense, even flirtatious bond with the father
A mother who was not totally there for her son
A distant, strict and critical patriarchal father
A strong mother who raised a good, obedient boy
A mother who adored her son and showered him with attention
questions.explain: Each projection comes from the influence of the parent of the opposite sex, the same source Greene gives for the anima and animus.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each gender projection type to Greene's description of the projector's anima or animus.
pairs: A seductive animus with an aggressive, masculine edge
A dreamy, introspective and moody anima
A quite angry and resentful animus
An anima with a sharp, recriminating edge
questions.explain: Greene ends most type descriptions by characterizing the inner figure that the projection reveals.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each example from the Law of Gender Rigidity to the projection type it illustrates.
questions.explain: Greene uses one real life and two novels, Proust's Swann's Way and Eliot's Middlemarch, to illustrate these three types.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each gender projection type to Greene's remedy for it.
pairs: Stop mythologizing the father and see the damage he caused
Accept a real woman's flaws and find the muse within
Practice saying no and breaking some rules in small steps
Build confidence through projects, a business or a craft
Learn to comfort and soothe himself
questions.explain: In each case the cure is to stop seeking outside what was repressed inside and to develop it directly.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these gender projection types by who usually does the projecting, according to Greene.

items.t: The Elusive Woman of Perfection
The Fallen Woman
The Woman to Worship Him
The Devilish Romantic
The Lovable Rebel
The Superior Man

questions.explain: Each type is named for the fantasy figure: men project idealized women, and women project idealized men.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put the six gender projection types in the order Greene presents them.
items: The Devilish Romantic
The Elusive Woman of Perfection
The Lovable Rebel
The Fallen Woman
The Superior Man
The Woman to Worship Him
questions.explain: Greene alternates female and male projections, starting with the Devilish Romantic and ending with the Woman to Worship Him.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these are among the three ways Greene says you must use knowledge of the gender projection types?
options: Be attentive to how others project their needs and fantasies onto you
Judge which of your parents was most to blame
Gain access to other people's unconscious and see their anima and animus in action
Recognize in yourself any tendency toward one of these projections
Deliberately trigger projections in others to win their love
questions.explain: Greene lists self-recognition, insight into others, and awareness of being projected upon; manipulating or blaming is not among them.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A man keeps becoming obsessed with women he barely knows, sure each will give him what he has always missed, yet he loses interest as soon as he gets close. Which projection type fits him?
options: The Elusive Woman of Perfection
The Woman to Worship Him
The Superior Man
The Fallen Woman
questions.explain: Imagining perfection in near strangers and moving on once reality sets in is the Elusive Woman pattern. The Woman to Worship Him man instead pushes a woman into a mothering role.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, Greene asks us to look at the midlife crisis from a different angle. What does he reframe it as?
options: A crisis of identity
A crisis of faith
A crisis of ambition
A crisis of physical decline
questions.explain: Greene treats it as a crisis of identity: we have become too rigidly identified with our gender role and the mask we present.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says that at a certain point in life, often near the age of ____, we go through what is known as a midlife crisis.
questions.explain: Work feels mechanical and relationships have lost their spirit, so we crave change.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: How does Greene explain the midlife crisis as a crisis of identity in the Law of Gender Rigidity?
questions.a: As children we had a fluid sense of self and absorbed a wide range of energies, but in youth we trimmed this to form a cohesive social self, largely by repressing masculine or feminine sides. Over the years the gender role grows more fixed, and we sense we have lost something essential and our creative energies dry up. The source is within: we are imbalanced and too rigidly identified with our mask, and at some point we inwardly rebel at this loss.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Why does Greene say that a new career, relationship or bit of danger fails to cure a midlife crisis?
options: Because people in midlife cannot really change their habits
Because such changes are always too risky to succeed
Because they give a short-term jolt but leave the inner source of the problem untouched
Because the crisis is caused mainly by physical aging
questions.explain: We naturally look outward, but the crisis comes from within, so the malaise returns after the jolt fades.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put these stages in the development of identity in the order Greene describes them.
items: As children we have a fluid sense of self
In youth we shape a cohesive social self by repressing parts of ourselves
Into our twenties we keep adjusting the identity and enjoy many possibilities
Over the years our gender role grows more and more fixed
We sense we have lost something essential and rebel inwardly
questions.explain: Greene moves from childhood openness, through the forging of a social identity, to the rigidity that triggers the midlife crisis.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In primitive cultures, Greene says, the wisest man or woman in the tribe was the ____, the healer who could communicate with the spirit world.
questions.explain: The male shaman listened to an inner wife and the female shaman to an inner husband.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, where did the power of the shaman come from?
options: From the shaman's physical strength and courage
From the depth of communication with an inner figure of the opposite sex
From the shaman's isolation from the rest of the tribe
From long training in the tribe's rituals
questions.explain: The shamans' power came from their communication with an inner woman or man, experienced as real, which Greene sees as a profound psychological truth.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the myths of many ancient cultures, Greene says, original humans were both male and female, so powerful that the gods feared them and split them in ____.
questions.explain: Greene cites Persian, Hebrew, Greek and Egyptian myths as reflecting the power of our original, undivided nature.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What benefits does Greene promise from returning to your original nature in the Law of Gender Rigidity?
questions.a: Relating more to the feminine or masculine parts within you unleashes energy that has been repressed and lets your mind recover its natural fluidity. You will understand and relate better to the opposite sex. And by ridding yourself of defensiveness about your gender role, you will feel secure in who you are.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: What deeply ingrained prejudice about the masculine and the feminine does Greene say we must first come to terms with, and what does he say is truly needed?
questions.a: For millennia men defined gender roles and judged feminine thinking as irrational and feminine action as weak and inferior, and these judgments still have deep roots even as outward equality has progressed. Many women have internalized them and think equality means being as tough and aggressive as men. What is truly needed is to see masculine and feminine as equal in potential reasoning power and strength of action, but in different ways.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene argues that the masculine style of thinking is truly more rational and scientific than the feminine style.
questions.explain: He says it has long been seen that way, but this does not reflect reality; the greatest scientists mixed both styles.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these traits does Greene give for the masculine style of thinking?
options: Letting solutions cook over time until they come in intuitive flashes
Looking for contrasts in order to categorize and label things
Thinking in a linear sequence of steps
Preferring specialization and digging deep into one thing
Focusing on the overall gestalt and how the parts connect
questions.explain: Categorizing, linear thinking and specialization are masculine traits; attention to the whole and slow-cooking intuition belong to the feminine style.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says feminine thinking likes to focus on the whole, how the parts connect to one another, the overall ____.
questions.explain: Instead of freezing phenomena to analyze parts, the feminine style looks at relationships and organic processes.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Put these steps of the feminine style of solving a puzzle in the order Greene describes.
items: Meditate on several aspects of the problem
Absorb the patterns
Let answers come over time, as if they needed to be cooked
Hidden connections suddenly become visible in intuitive flashes
questions.explain: Greene describes a slow, absorbing process that ends in intuitive insight, in contrast to the masculine step-by-step analysis.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these into the masculine and feminine styles of thinking, as Greene describes them.

items.t: Takes things apart like a machine
Linear, following a sequence of steps
Looks from the outside with emotional detachment
Likes building elaborate structures
Focuses on how one thing grows into another
Connects different fields of knowledge
Wants to understand a culture from within
Sensitive to information from the senses

questions.explain: Greene contrasts analysis, sequence and detachment with attention to wholes, growth, connection and the inside view.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these people does Greene cite as great scientists or thinkers who blended masculine and feminine styles of thinking?
options: Margaret Mead
Albert Einstein
Miyamoto Musashi
Louis Pasteur
Hannibal
questions.explain: Pasteur, Einstein and Mead mixed analysis with intuition or inside experience. Hannibal illustrates the masculine style of action and Musashi the patient feminine style of action.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each figure to how Greene says they blended masculine and feminine styles of thinking.
pairs: Opened his mind to many explanations and let them cook
Credited his discoveries to intuitions after long hours of thinking
Combined abstract models with months living inside a culture
Analyzes a company's parts and also its spirit and gestalt
questions.explain: Each pairs rigorous analysis with the feminine capacity for connection, intuition or an inside view.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, why does Greene cite Warren Buffett?
options: As a businessman whose cold analysis shows the power of the masculine style
As a leader who uses fear to keep his company cohesive
As an example of someone who relies only on intuition
As someone who analyzes a company's parts in depth and also senses its overall gestalt
questions.explain: Buffett looks at a company from both outside and inside, weighing intangibles like how employees relate that most businesspeople ignore.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, how should someone who leans toward the masculine style of thinking create balance?
questions.a: They should widen the fields they look at, finding connections between different forms of knowledge, and consider more possibilities, giving more time to deliberation and freer associations. They must take seriously the intuitions that come after long deliberation and not discount the value of emotion in thinking, since without excitement and inspiration thinking becomes stale and lifeless.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, how should someone who leans toward the feminine style of thinking create balance?
questions.a: They need to focus and dig into specific problems, tamping down the urge to widen the search and multitask, and find pleasure in boring into one aspect and reconstructing a causal chain. Instead of seeing structure and order as dull, they should pay deep attention to the structure of a book, argument or project, since clear structure gives material its power to influence. Sometimes they must force themselves to gain greater emotional distance from a problem.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene quotes Hannibal to capture the masculine style of action: I will either find a way or ____ a way.
questions.explain: The masculine tendency is to push through obstacles, stay on the offensive and take risks.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene cites Queen Elizabeth I's response to the Spanish armada as an example of what?
options: The masculine style of attacking first to keep the initiative
A failure caused by too much hesitation
The feminine style of waiting to see, and letting bad weather destroy the enemy
A leader who relied on fear to keep her advisers loyal
questions.explain: She would not commit to a strategy until she knew when the armada was launched and the weather, slowing it and letting the weather destroy it with minimal loss of life.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: True or false: Greene says Queen Elizabeth I did not commit to a strategy against the armada until she knew when it was launched and what the weather was.
questions.explain: Her wait-and-see strategy illustrates the feminine style of action, which lays traps instead of charging forward.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene says that to Chinese strategists, ____, or nonaction, is often the height of wisdom.
questions.explain: Aggressive action is seen as foolish because it narrows one's options; the West, by contrast, tends to judge this style as weak.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Which of these qualities does Greene say give the feminine style of action its tremendous strength?
options: Resilience
Patience
Flexibility
Speed of attack
Independence from allies
questions.explain: Greene names patience, resilience and flexibility. Speed and independence belong to the masculine style, while the feminine style values interdependent relationships.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: In the Law of Gender Rigidity, why does Greene argue that the feminine style of action is not weak?
questions.a: In the West the feminine style of withdrawing, avoiding conflict and laying traps is instinctively judged timid, but other cultures see it differently: to Chinese strategists wu-wei, nonaction, is often the height of wisdom, and aggression narrows one's options. The style contains patience, resilience and flexibility. The samurai Miyamoto Musashi held that standing back and letting the opponent tire himself out before counterattacking was critical to success.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Sort these into the masculine and feminine styles of action, as Greene describes them.

items.t: Push through obstacles
Stay on the offensive and take risks
Keep independence and room to maneuver
Withdraw first to contemplate the options
Win without having to go to battle
Lay traps for the enemy
Focus on interdependent relationships

questions.explain: Greene contrasts attack and independence with withdrawal, traps and attention to alliances.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Match each figure to what Greene uses them to illustrate in the Law of Gender Rigidity.
pairs: Pushing through obstacles: find a way or make a way
Waiting to see before acting against an invasion
Letting the opponent tire himself out before counterattacking
A leader made stronger by considering each man's emotions
questions.explain: Hannibal shows the masculine style of action, Elizabeth and Musashi the strength of the feminine style, and Shackleton the value of empathy in male leadership.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: A hard-charging executive in her forties finds her career blocked and feels pressure to make a dramatic move at once. What would Greene advise for someone with her aggressive, masculine style?
options: Withdraw and reflect on her needs, strengths and true interests before deciding
Act immediately, since hesitation shows weakness
Copy whatever her most aggressive rival is doing
Hand all her decisions over to a trusted mentor
questions.explain: Greene says that if you are blocked later in life you must learn the power of withdrawing and reflecting, even for weeks or months, before any important decision.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: Greene quotes a French saying for the value of withdrawing before acting: reculer pour mieux ____, step back in order to leap forward.
questions.explain: He offers it to those with a masculine style who are blocked in their careers, noting some great leaders honed their best ideas in prison.

questions.unitTitle: Reconnect to the Masculine or Feminine Within You
questions.q: According to Greene, how should someone with the feminine style of action approach conflict?
questions.a: They should accustom themselves to degrees of conflict so that any avoidance is strategic rather than fearful, starting with baby steps such as confronting people in small everyday ways. They must drop the need always to consider the other side's feelings, since some bad people must be thwarted, and get comfortable saying no.
